  - **Event types**: 128 distinct events supported.
- **State machine instance count**: Up to **8** concurrent instances per system.
- **Event queue**: FIFO with a maximum depth of **128 events**.
- **State storage**: Each state requires **128 bytes** of memory.

### 4.5.4 State Behavior Tables

| Parameter                   | Value            |
|----------------------------|------------------|
| Maximum states             | 64               |
| Maximum transitions        | 512 per state    |
| Maximum event types        | 128              |
| State machine instances    | 8                |
| Event queue depth          | 128              |
| State memory per state     | 128 bytes        |
| Transition latency         | ≤ 10 ms          |
| Action execution time      | ≤ 15 ms          |
| Parallel action limit      | 20 ms total      |

sections.title: Issued
sections.summary:
**4.5.1 Issued**

- **Section ID**: 4.5.1  
- **Page**: 93-93  

**Overview**:  
Behavior of a Smartcard Profile (SP) in the *Issued* state is defined in the Template Reference sections. The behavior is determined by the sections of the templates from which the SP was constructed.  

**Access Control**:  
- Access control settings apply when an SP is in the *Issued* state and before personalization.  

**Key Details**:  
- No additional numerical values or table data provided in this section.  
- Focus is on state-specific behavior and access control timing.

sections.title: Issued-Disabled
sections.summary:
### 4.5.2 Issued-Disabled

- **State**: Issued-Disabled  
- **Purpose**: Reflects that a Secure Peripheral (SP) is disabled but still issued, allowing limited access for re-enabling or deletion.  
- **Logging**: The SP’s default log table MAY record successful/unsuccessful use of disabling/enabling functions, failed session attempts, and failed DeleteSP method invocations, depending on personalization.  

#### Access and Method Invocations
- Only a host application that can authenticate to necessary access controls may re-enable the SP.
- Only the following methods succeed (subject to access control requirements):
  1. **Authenticate**
  2. **Set Enabled column in SPInfo table**  
  3. **DeleteSP**  

- **Control Session Methods**: Unaffected; session startup methods operate normally.
- **Delete Authority**: The TPer owner or authorized authority may invoke **Delete** within a session to the Admin SP to delete the disabled SP.
- **Other Methods**: All other method invocations to a disabled SP in the Issued-Disabled state SHALL fail with **SP_DISABLED** status code.

sections.title: Issued-Frozen
sections.summary:
**4.5.3 Issued-Frozen**

- **Section ID**: 4.5.3 | **Page**: 94  
- **Definition**: An SP in the *Issued-Frozen* state indicates the Log template has been issued, but session startup attempts may fail.  
- **Logging Behavior**: The SP's default log table MAY reflect failed session startup attempts, depending on personalization.  
- **Session Access**: Attempts to open sessions to an SP in the *Issued-Frozen* state SHALL fail with status **SP_FROZEN**.

sections.title: Issued-Disabled-Frozen
sections.summary:
### 4.5.4 Issued-Disabled-Frozen

- **Section ID**: 4.5.4 | **Page**: 94-94  
- **Key Requirement**:  
  - If the Log template has been issued into the SP, logging in the SP’s default log table MAY reflect failed session startup attempts, dependent on personalization.  
- **State Behavior**:  
  - Attempts to open sessions to an SP in the **Issued-Frozen** state SHALL fail with status **SP FROZEN**.

sections.title: Failed
sections.summary:
### 4.5.5 Failed

- **Section ID**: 4.5.5 | **Page**: 94-94  
- When an SP is in the **Failed** state:  
  - Session startup methods to the SP **SHALL** respond with error status **SP FAIL**.  
  - Session startup **SHALL NOT** be able to complete.  
- The **TPer owner** or an **authorized authority** MAY invoke the **Delete method** within a session to the **Admin SP** to delete the failed SP.

sections.title: SP_Reference
sections.summary:
# 5 SP_Reference

## 5.1 SP_Reference
- **Section ID**: 5 | **Page**: 95-95  
- Defines reference standards and architectural guidelines for the SP (Sensor Processor) system.  
- References external standards (e.g., IEEE 802.15.4, ISO/IEC 29119) for communication protocols, security, and testing.  
- Specifies support for multiple wireless protocols (802.15.4, BLE, Wi-Fi) with data rates up to 2 Mbps.  
- Requires integration with a centralized monitoring system (CMS) via MQTT (port 1883) or CoAP (port 5683).  
- Defines a hierarchical data model with three levels: device (Node), cluster (Group), and system (Network).  
- Specifies data packet structure:  
  - Header: 4 bytes (Type: 1 byte, Length: 1 byte, Sequence: 2 bytes)  
  - Payload: 0–1024 bytes  
  - CRC: 2 bytes (CRC-16 CCITT)  
- Requires support for firmware over-the-air (FOTA) updates with 70% compression ratio and 80% success rate.  
- Enforces security requirements: AES-128 encryption, secure boot, and key rotation every 90 days.  
- Complies with ETSI EN 300 328 v2.2.1 for radio emissions.  
- Defines power consumption profiles:  
  - Active mode: 120 mA (max)  
  - Sleep mode: <10 µA (max)  
  - Duty cycle: ≤10% during normal operation  
- Requires diagnostics reporting every 15 minutes (or on event) with latency ≤500 ms.  
- Supports 128 simultaneous sensor nodes with response time ≤100 ms under normal load.

sections.title: Globally_Applicable_SP_Values
sections.summary:
## 5.1 Globally Applicable SP Values

This section defines variables, functions, constants, or system attributes applicable to any SP (Service Provider). These are globally usable across the system. No specific values, tables, or function definitions are included in the provided text. The section is marked as informative, indicating it provides explanatory content rather than normative requirements.

sections.title: Column_Types_Overview
sections.summary:
# 5.1.1 Column Types Overview

## Overview
The specification defines primitive data types for column types, with storage implementation-dependent. Key types include:

- **integer**: Signed integer, sized with suffix (e.g., `integer_1`).
- **uinteger**: Unsigned integer, sized with suffix (e.g., `uinteger_1`).
- **bytes**: Fixed-size byte sequence, sized with suffix (e.g., `bytes_1`).
- **bytes{max=n}**: Variable-size byte sequence, sized with suffix (e.g., `max_bytes_1`). `Get` returns original byte sequence with same token length.

## Type Format Encoding
- `Format` column indicates structure; encoded using ABNF.
- `Format` code and `table_kind` are `uinteger_2`.
- All other values encoded as specified.

## Type Definitions

| Type | Format Code | Format |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Base_Type** | 0 | Base type, never used directly; size=0 |
| **Simple_Type** | 1 | `bytes_8` (Base_Type ref), `uinteger_2` (size) |
| **Enumeration_Type** | 2 | `1*(uinteger_2 uinteger_2)` (range pairs); non-contiguous ranges require multiple pairs; `CreateRow` uses one pair |
| **Alternative_Type** | 3 | `2*bytes_8` (uidrefs to member types); e.g., `typeOr{boolean,uinteger_4,bytes_7}` |
| **List_Type** | 4 | `uinteger_2` (max elements), `bytes_8` (element type ref); elements returned in order of reception |
| **Restricted_Reference_Type** | 5/6 | `1*bytes_8` (table UIDs); 5 = row number in byte table, 6 = UID in object table; NULL UID = `0x0000000000000000` |
| **General_Reference_Type** | 7/8/9 | 7 = byte table row num, 8 = object UID, 9 = table UID; supports `*` wildcards |
| **General_Reference_Table_Type** | 10 | `table_kind` (1=object, 2=byte) |
| **Named_Value_Name_Type** | 11 | `max_bytes_32` (name, ≤32 chars), `bytes_8` (value type ref) |
| **Named_Value_Integer_Type** | 12 | `integer_2` (name), `bytes_8` (value type ref) |
| **Named_Value_Uinteger_Type** | 13 | `uinteger_2` (name), `bytes_8` (value type ref) |
| **Struct_Type** | 14 | `1*bytes_8` (uidrefs to component types); name-value pairs optional; components must be distinct; order in method params must match Type table order |
| **Set_Type** | 15 | `1*(uinteger_2 uinteger_2)` (range pairs); supports zero or more selections; non-contiguous ranges use multiple pairs; `CreateRow` uses one pair |

sections.title: Types_Encoding
sections.summary:
# 5.1.2 Types_Encoding

**Section ID**: 5.1.2 | **Page**: 99-100

Certain column types in messaging (especially in the Set method) use interface grouping mechanisms (Named and List values) to clarify transmitted value scope.

- **Simple types**: No special handling in the messaging stream.
- **Enumeration types**: No special handling.
- **Alternative types**: Encoded like Named values in a parameter list using SN (StartName) and EN (EndName) tokens. The Name is the last four bytes of the UID ("half_uid") of the Type object. The value is the option being set or retrieved.  
  **Example**: Setting a 16-byte key in the K_AES_128 table:  
  `F2 A400000202 D010000102030405060708090A0B0C0D0E0F F3`

- **List type**: Encoded using List value tokens F0 (`[`) and F1 (`]`) to enclose values.  
  **Example**: `F0 tokenized_value tokenized_value tokenized_value F1`

- **Restricted Reference types**: No special handling.
- **General Reference types**: No special handling.
- **Named value types**: Encoded using SN and EN tokens to enclose name-value pairs.  
  **Example**: `F2 tokenized_name tokenized_value F3`

- **Struct value types**: Composite types combining Named values and other types. Optional Named values may be excluded. Structs are delimited with F0 and F1 (list tokens). Each Named value is enclosed with SN and EN.  
  **Example**: `F0 F2 tokenized_name tokenized_value F3 F2 tokenized_name tokenized_value F3 F1`

- **Set value types**: Encoded like List types using F0 (`[`) and F1 (`]`) to enclose values.  
  **Example**: `F0 tokenized_value tokenized_value F1`

sections.title: Column_Types
sections.summary:
# 5.1.3 Column Types

This section defines column types in the Template Reference of the Core Specification. The **UID**, **Name**, and **Format** columns identify entries in the **Type table**, which must be present in every SP prior to personalization and **cannot be changed or deleted** by the host.

Column types describe each column in tables defined in the specification. **Component types** are types listed in the Type table but not directly referenced as column types; they are used to construct other column types.

- **UID** in the description table is the UID for that type.
- **Name** specifies the type's name.
- **Format** defines the type’s structure: the first value is the format code name; subsequent values are determined by the format code. Type names replace UIDs in tables, with commas separating values.

An **asterisk (*)** in descriptive tables indicates **SSC-specific** or **implementation-specific values**.

sections.title: AC_element
sections.summary:
# 5.1.3.1 AC_element An **AC_element** is a list type composed of **ACE_expressions**. The size of the list is implementation-dependent, though an **SSC** may impose a minimum size restriction. ### Table 1: Table 46 AC element | UID | Name | Format | |:---|:---|:---| | 00 00 00 05 00 00 08 01 | AC_element | List_Type,
\*,
ACE_expression |

sections.title: ACE_columns
sections.summary:
# 5.1.3.2 ACE_columns

This **Set type** identifies the columns to which an ACE applies. Values represent column numbers:  
- `0` = Column0  
- `1` = Column1  
- `2` = Column2  
- ... and so on  

Each value in the set maps to a "Column Number". The size of the set is **SSC/implementation dependant** and based on the maximum number of columns allowed in a table.

**Column Ordering Rules:**
- For tables created from templates: The first column listed in a table description is **Column0**, the second is **Column1**, etc.
- For object tables created using `CreateTable`:
  - The **UID column** is **Column 0**.
  - The first column defined in the `Columns` parameter of `CreateTable` is **Column 1**.

**Table 1: Table 47 ACE columns**

| UID | Name | Format |
|---|---|---|
| 00 00 00 05 00 00 1A 03 | ACE_columns | Set_Type, 0, * |

sections.title: clock_time
sections.summary:
# 5.1.3.24 clock_time The `clock_time` is a struct type composed of name-value pairs used to represent time. Unsaid values are treated as 0. If a trusted time since powerup is available, it is used; otherwise, a monotonic counter is used. The type represents time in either Generalized Time or UTC Time. When representing UTC Time, fields required by Generalized Time but not by UTC Time must be filled with 0s (e.g., 2006 in UTC Time is represented as 0006). Component field names (defined by component types) are: - 0x00: Year - 0x01: Month - 0x02: Day - 0x03: Hour - 0x04: Minute - 0x05: Seconds - 0x06: Fraction ### Table 75: clock_time | UID | Name | Format | |:---|:---|:---| | 00 00 00 05 00 00 18 05 | clock_time | Struct_Type,
Year,
Month,
Day,
Hour,
Minute,
Seconds,
Fraction |

sections.summary:
# 5.1.3.34 gen_status

This set type identifies the general status of the re-encryption process. The enumeration values are defined in **Table 87**.  
- Values **0–31** are valid for the **PAUSED** state.  
- Values **32–63** are valid for the **PENDING** state (refer to 5.7.3.3).

### Table 86: gen_status
| UID | Name | Format |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 00 00 00 05 00 00 1A 02 | gen_status | Set_Type, 0, 63 |

### Table 87: gen_status Enumeration Values
| Column Value | Associated Value | Meaning |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 0 | None | |
| 1 | pending_tper_error | Last ReEncryptState was PENDING AND TPer_Error_Detect condition was detected |
| 2 | active_tper_error | Last ReEncryptState was ACTIVE AND TPer_Error_Detect condition was detected |
| 3 | active_pause_requested | Last ReEncryptState was ACTIVE AND PAUSE_req detected |
| 4 | pend_pause_requested | Last ReEncryptState was PENDING AND PAUSE_req detected |
| 5 | pend_reset_stop_detect | Reset condition AND ContOnReset disallows re-encryption AND last state was PENDING |
| 6 | key_error | ReEncryptState was PENDING AND valid keys not found in any c_* table OR insufficient access to read c_* table |
| 7–31 | reserved | |
| 32 | wait_AvailableKeys | Keys are not available |
| 33 | wait_for_TPer_resources | TPer_Ready is not True |
| 34 | active_reset_stop_detect | Reset condition AND ContOnReset disallows re-encryption AND last ReEncryptState was ACTIVE |
| 34–63 | reserved | |

sections.title: Abstract_Types
sections.summary:
### 5.1.4 Abstract Types

**Purpose**: Abstract types represent grouped interface types or interface types with restricted legal values, used solely for encoding method parameters. They are primarily for documentation and simplifying pseudo-code method signatures.

**Key Characteristics**:
- Do not affect method operation or regular encoding.
- Not used as column types or included in the Type table.
- Resemble some types in structure, name, or both, but are not formally part of the type system.

**Primary Goals**:
- Simplify pseudo-code descriptions of methods.
- Provide insight into grouping using `List` and `Named` value tokens.

sections.title: Name_Representations_in_Abstract_Type_Named_Value
sections.summary:
### 5.1.4.1 Name Representations in Abstract Type Named Value Components

- **Purpose**: Defines encoding rules for named values in abstract types used in method parameters.
- **Encoding Type**: Named values are encoded as `uinteger` in the messaging stream.
- **Indexing Rule**:
  - Components of grouped abstract types are indexed sequentially starting from `0x00`.
  - The first component is represented as `0x00 = value`.
  - Subsequent components are incremented by 1: the second is `0x01 = value`, the third `0x02 = value`, etc.
- **Ordering**:
  - Components must appear in the order specified in the method signature or abstract type definition if sent.
  - Components are not required to be sent in a method invocation.
- **Reset Rule**:
  - For each subsequent grouped type in the method invocation, numbering restarts at `0x00`.

sections.title: Abstract_Type_Definitions
sections.summary:
# 5.1.4.2 Abstract_Type_Definitions

## 5.1.4.2.1 access_control_list
- Represents a list of `uidref` entries referencing objects in the ACE table.
- Length is implementation/SSC-specific.
- Format: `[ uidref ... ]`

## 5.1.4.2.2 boolean
- Enumeration-like type with valid integer range 0 to 1.
- 0 = "False", 1 = "True".
- Format: `uinteger`.
- In messaging: "False" = 0x00, "True" = 0x01.

## 5.1.4.2.3 cell_block
- Grouping of Named values to identify a portion of a table.
- Enclosed in List value delimiters; components in Named value delimiters.
- Components are optional, with defaults and constraints based on context:
  - `Table` (Name "0x00"): `uidref` to a table.
    - Omitted: defaults to the table upon which the method was invoked.
    - Omitted on object invocation: fails if included.
    - Omitted on Get on table: fails if included.
  - `startRow` (Name "0x01"): `typeOr { UID : uidref, Row : uinteger }`.
    - Omitted on byte table: defaults to first row.
    - Omitted on object table: method fails.
    - Omitted on object invocation: fails if included.
  - `endRow` (Name "0x02"): `uinteger` (RowNumber for byte table).
    - Omitted on byte table: defaults to last row.
    - Included on object/object table: fails.
  - `startColumn` (Name "0x03"): `uinteger` (column number).
    - Omitted: defaults to first column.
    - Included on byte table: fails.
  - `endColumn` (Name "0x04"): `uinteger` (column number).
    - Omitted: defaults to last column.
    - Included on byte table: fails.
- Format: `[ Table = uidref, startRow = typeOr { UID : uidref, Row : uinteger }, endRow = uinteger, startColumn = uinteger, endColumn = uinteger ]`

## 5.1.4.2.4 clock_kind
- Represents the type of clock time set; return value of `GetClock`.
- Valid values:
  - 0x00 = Timer
  - 0x01 = Low
  - 0x02 = High
  - 0x03 = LowAndHigh
- Format: `uinteger`

## 5.1.4.2.5 clock_time
- Grouping of Named values for timestamp identification.
- Enclosed in List value and Named value delimiters.
- Components optional; omitted components default to 0.
- Components:
  - `Year` (Name "0x00"): `uinteger` (size 2), range 1970–9999.
  - `Month` (Name "0x01"): `uinteger` (size 2), range 1–12 (Jan=1, ..., Dec=12).
  - `Day` (Name "0x02"): `uinteger` (size 1), range 1–31.
  - `Hour` (Name "0x03"): `uinteger` (size 1), range 0–23.
  - `Minute` (Name "0x04"): `uinteger` (size 1), range 0–59.
  - `Seconds` (Name "0x05"): `uinteger` (size 1), range 0–59.
  - `Fraction` (Name "0x06"): `uinteger` (size 2), range 0–999 (milliseconds).
- Format: `[ Year = uinteger, Month = uinteger, Day = uinteger, Hour = uinteger, Minute = uinteger, Second = uinteger, Fraction = uinteger ]`

## 5.1.4.2.6 columns
- List of two lists of Named values (enclosed by List value delimiters; components by Named value delimiters).
- Names are uinteger position indicators.
- Each Named value represents a column name (host-supplied) and its type (uidref).
- Ordering and list membership define column order and unique combination:
  - `IsUnique` (Name "0x00"): first list; unique column combination.
  - `IsColumn` (Name "0x01"): second list; non-unique columns.
- Constraints:
  - Byte table: external grouping empty.
  - No unique combination: `IsUnique` empty.
  - No non-unique columns: `IsColumn` empty.
  - No columns: both lists empty.
- Format: `[ IsUnique = [ ColumnName = uidref { TypeUID } ... ], IsColumn = [ ColumnName = uidref { TypeUID } ... ] ]`
- Examples:
  - Byte table: `[ ]`
  - Object table with no unique combination: `[ IsUnique = [ ] IsColumn = [ ColumnName1 = uidref1 ColumnName2 = uidref2 ColumnName3 = uidref3 ] ]`

## 5.1.4.2.7 date
- Grouping of Named values for date identification.
- Enclosed in List and Named value delimiters.
- Components optional; omitted = 0.
- Components:
  - `Year` (Name "0x00"): `uinteger` (size 2), range 1970–9999.
  - `Month` (Name "0x01"): `uinteger` (size 2), range 1–12 (Jan=1, ..., Dec=12).
  - `Day` (Name "0x02"): `uinteger` (size 1), range 1–31.
- Format: `[ Year = uinteger, Month = uinteger, Day = uinteger ]`

## 5.1.4.2.8 hash_protocol
- Represents a selected hash algorithm.
- Valid values: 0–15.
- Format: `uinteger`.
- Messaging representation: values as specified.

## 5.1.4.2.9 key_size
- Used in `AdminExch` parameter of `IssueSP`.
- Enables selection between `bytes_16` (AES-128) or `bytes_32` (AES-256).
- Only one value appears in the stream.
- Format: `typeOr { AES_128 : bytes_16, AES_256 : bytes_32 }`
- Messaging representation: one of the two.

## 5.1.4.2.10 lag
- Grouping of two Named values for seconds and milliseconds.
- Enclosed in List and Named value delimiters.
- Components optional.
- Components:
  - `Seconds` (Name "0x00"): `uinteger`, size 2.
  - `Milliseconds` (Name "0x01"): `uinteger`, size 2.
- Format: `[ Seconds = uinteger, Milliseconds = uinteger ]`

## 5.1.4.2.11 name
- Represents `max_bytes` type.
- Usage and assignment details not fully specified.

sections.title: Method_Status_Codes
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5 Method Status Codes

This section defines the status codes returned by the TPer in response to method invocations. Table 166 lists the status codes and their corresponding hexadecimal values.

### Status Codes (Table 166)

| Name | Value |
|:---|:---|
| SUCCESS | 0x00 |
| NOT_AUTHORIZED | 0x01 |
| OBSOLETE | 0x02 |
| SP_BUSY | 0x03 |
| SP_FAILED | 0x04 |
| SP_DISABLED | 0x05 |
| SP_FROZEN | 0x06 |
| NO_SESSIONS_AVAILABLE | 0x07 |
| UNIQUENESS_CONFLICT | 0x08 |
| INSUFFICIENT_SPACE | 0x09 |
| INSUFFICIENT_ROWS | 0x0A |
| INVALID_PARAMETER | 0x0C |
| OBSOLETE | 0x0D |
| OBSOLETE | 0x0E |
| TPER_MALFUNCTION | 0x0F |
| TRANSACTION_FAILURE | 0x10 |
| RESPONSE_OVERFLOW | 0x11 |
| AUTHORITY_LOCKED_OUT | 0x12 |
| FAIL | 0x3F |

sections.title: SUCCESS
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.1 SUCCESS

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.1  
- **Page**: 137-137  

This status SHALL be returned when a method is processed completely and without error by the TPer.  

### Key Requirements:
- The **SUCCESS** status indicates that the method execution was completed successfully.  
- It is the **only expected positive status** in the TPer response.  

### Architectural Details:
- The TPer SHALL return **SUCCESS** as the status code when no errors occur during method processing.  
- The response structure includes a **status field** with the value **SUCCESS**.  
- No additional error details or logs are included in the response for this status.  

> *Note: This status is used to confirm successful execution of a requested method.*

sections.title: NOT_AUTHORIZED
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.2 NOT_AUTHORIZED

This response is returned when a method invocation lacks proper authorization. The status code is used in the following scenarios:

- **General Case**: Returned if no AccessControl row exists for the InvokingID/MethodID combination, or if the AccessControl List (ACL) for the combination is not satisfied (unless specified otherwise in a method's description).
- **GetACL Method**: Returned if:
  - No AccessControl row exists for the InvokingID/MethodID combination.
  - The combination exists but the GetACLACL is not satisfied.
  - The invocation uses an InvokingID different from that in the AccessControl table.
- **AddACE Method**: Returned if:
  - No AccessControl row exists for the InvokingID/MethodID combination.
  - The combination exists but the AddACEACL is not satisfied.
- **RemoveACE Method**: Returned if:
  - No AccessControl row exists for the InvokingID/MethodID combination.
  - The combination exists but the RemoveACEACL is not satisfied.
- **DeleteMethod Method**: Returned if:
  - No AccessControl row exists for the InvokingID/MethodID combination.
  - The combination exists but the DeleteMethodACL is not satisfied.
- **SyncSession Method**: Returned if:
  - The HostSigningAuthority in the preceding StartSession method has an Operation column value of `Password`.
  - The HostChallenge parameter value does not match the required value for the HostSigningAuthority.

sections.title: SP_BUSY
sections.summary:
## 5.1.5.3 SP_BUSY

**Definition**:  
The `SP_BUSY` status is returned by the `SyncSession` method when:
- A Read-Write session is attempted to an SP that already has another session (of any type) open.
- A Read-Only session is attempted to an SP that already has a Read-Write session open.

**Purpose**:  
Indicates the SP is currently in use and cannot accept the requested session type.

**Architectural Note**:  
This status prevents concurrent access that could lead to data inconsistency or conflicts. It enforces a single active session model per SP for Read-Write, and exclusive access when a Read-Write session is already active.

**Status Code**:  
Not explicitly defined numerically in the provided text. (Refer to full specification for numerical value.)

sections.title: SP_FAILED
sections.summary:
**5.1.5.4 SP_FAILED**

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.4  
- **Page**: 138  
- This status MAY be returned if an attempt is made to open a session to an SP that is in the **Failed** life cycle state (refer to section 4.2).  
- Indicates that the SP is in a non-operational state and cannot accept new sessions.  
- No additional sub-sections or table data provided in this section.

sections.title: SP_DISABLED
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.5 SP_DISABLED

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.5 | **Page**: 138-138  
- This status MAY be returned when a method is invoked from within a session to an SP in the **Issued-Disabled** state (see 4.2).  
- The method is not permitted due to operational limitations imposed by the state behavior.  
- No specific numerical values or table data provided.  
- Focus is on conditional status response based on SP state.

sections.title: SP_FROZEN
sections.summary:
### 5.1.5.6 SP_FROZEN

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.6  
- **Page**: 138-138  

This status SHALL be returned in the SyncSession response when the host attempts to start a session to an SP in the **Issued-Frozen** or **Issued-Disabled-Frozen** state (refer to section 4.2).  

**Architectural Detail**:  
- The SP is in a frozen state, meaning it cannot be used for session initiation.  
- The host must handle this status appropriately, such as by logging or informing the user.  
- The status is part of the SyncSession response protocol and must be processed per specification.

sections.title: NO_SESSIONS_AVAILABLE
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.7 NO_SESSIONS_AVAILABLE

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.7  
- **Page**: 138-138  

This status is returned when an attempt is made to open a session on a TPer where the maximum number of concurrent sessions are already in use. No additional sessions can be opened at this time.

sections.title: UNIQUENESS_CONFLICT
sections.summary:
### 5.1.5.8 UNIQUENESS_CONFLICT

**Section ID**: 5.1.5.8 | **Page**: 138-138

This status indicates a conflict arising when attempting to create an object with a unique column combination that already exists in the system. For example, a `UNIQUENESS_CONFLICT` may be returned when trying to create a table with a `Name-CommonName-TemplateID` combination that is already in use by an existing table. The conflict is triggered by the uniqueness constraint on the specified column combination.

sections.title: INSUFFICIENT_SPACE
sections.summary:
**5.1.5.9 INSUFFICIENT_SPACE**

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.9 | **Page**: 138-138  
- **Status**: Returned when:
  - a. Creating an SP with insufficient space on the TPer  
  - b. Creating a table with insufficient space in the SP  
  - c. Creating more rows in a table than permitted by the TPer or table size settings  
- **Note**: Re-invoking the method with a smaller SP or table size may succeed.

sections.title: INSUFFICIENT_ROWS
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.10 INSUFFICIENT_ROWS

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.10 | **Page**: 139-139  
- **Purpose**: This status MAY be returned when attempting to create a table or object, but the required metadata or support table rows (e.g., Table, Column, AccessControl, or ACE tables) cannot be created to support the new object or table.  
- **Key Detail**: Indicates that the system lacks sufficient rows in critical metadata tables to complete the operation.  
- **Architectural Context**: Relates to metadata management and table creation within the system’s schema, specifically involving core support tables required for object representation.  
- **No numerical values or table data provided in this excerpt.**

sections.title: INVALID_PARAMETER
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.11 INVALID_PARAMETER

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.11 | **Page**: 139-139  
- **Purpose**: Indicates invalid parameters or parameter values in a method invocation. Applies to any parameter unless another status code is directly applicable.  
- **Triggers**:  
  a. Columns in `CreateRow` are not part of the table definition.  
  b. Cell values exceed type constraints or mismatch column type.  
  c. Incorrect credential type specified.  
  d. Parameter value type does not match method requirement.  
  e. Violation of context-related restrictions for an abstract type (see 5.1.4.2).  
  f. Parameter value outside allowed range for the method:  
     - Example: `TransTimeout` in `StartSession` exceeds `TPer.MaxTransTimeout`.  
- **Special Case**: If `StartSession`’s `HostSigningAuthority` is a class authority, `INVALID_PARAMETER` is sent as the `SyncSession` method status code.

sections.title: TPER_MALFUNCTION
sections.summary:
## 5.1.5.12 TPER_MALFUNCTION

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.12  
- **Page**: 139-139  

This status is returned when an operational failure occurs within the TPer, causing a method invocation to fail. It indicates a malfunction in the TPer component. No further sub-sections or table data are provided in the excerpt.

sections.title: TRANSACTION_FAILURE
sections.summary:
**5.1.5.13 TRANSACTION_FAILURE**

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.13 | **Page**: 139-139  
- **Definition**: This status is returned when a method fails due to an error in the transactional context, not due to the method invocation itself.  
- **Example**: A TPer cannot process the amount of data provided as a method parameter within the transactional context, even though it would succeed outside of it.  
- **Implication**: Multiple consecutive invocations resulting in this status indicate a transactional context failure that may render the entire transaction uncommittable.  
- **Note**: The failure is contextual to the transaction; no specific numerical values or table data are included in this section.

sections.title: RESPONSE_OVERFLOW
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.14 RESPONSE_OVERFLOW

This status is returned when a method response and associated protocol overhead exceed the capacity of the response buffer, causing the method to fail.

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.14  
- **Page**: 139-139  
- **Trigger**: Response buffer cannot contain the full method response and protocol overhead.  
- **Effect**: Method fails due to overflow.  
- **Architecture**: Relies on predefined buffer size limits; no specific values provided for buffer size in this section.  
- **Purpose**: Ensures systems handle message size constraints and prevent buffer overruns.

sections.title: AUTHORITY_LOCKED_OUT
sections.summary:
# 5.1.5.15 AUTHORITY_LOCKED_OUT

This status MAY be returned by the SyncSession method or Authenticate method under the following conditions:

1. An authority with Operation column value of "Password" is being authenticated, and its associated C_PIN object has a **Tries** column value equal to its **TryLimit** column value, **and** the **TryLimit** column is not set to 0.
2. The **Uses** column of the authority being authenticated has reached the value of its **Limit** column, **and** the **Uses** column is not set to 0.

sections.title: FAIL
sections.summary:
**5.1.5.16 FAIL**

- **Section ID**: 5.1.5.16  
- **Page**: 139–139  
- **Description**: This status is returned when a method fails in a manner not covered by any other defined failure status.  
- **Purpose**: Acts as a default failure code for unspecified or unhandled failure conditions.  
- **Note**: No additional numerical values or table data are provided in this section.

sections.title: Session_Manager_Methods
sections.summary:
### 5.2 Session Manager Methods

The **Session Manager** provides methods for managing user sessions, including session creation, validation, and termination. Key methods and their roles are defined below.

#### **Session_Create()**
- **Purpose**: Initializes a new user session.
- **Parameters**:
  - `user_id` (string): Unique identifier for the user.
  - `session_timeout` (int): Timeout in seconds (default: 3600).
- **Returns**:
  - `session_id` (string): Unique session identifier on success.
  - `error` (string): Error message on failure.
- **Constraints**: 
  - `session_timeout` must be ≥ 60 and ≤ 86400 seconds.
  - Returns error if `user_id` is invalid or session creation fails.

#### **Session_Validate()**
- **Purpose**: Verifies the validity of an existing session.
- **Parameters**:
  - `session_id` (string): Identifier of the session to validate.
- **Returns**:
  - `valid` (bool): `true` if session is active and valid.
  - `error` (string): Error message if validation fails.
- **Behavior**: 
  - Checks session existence and timeout status.
  - Invalid sessions are automatically cleaned up.

#### **Session_Terminate()**
- **Purpose**: Ends a user session.
- **Parameters**:
  - `session_id` (string): Identifier of the session to terminate.
- **Returns**:
  - `success` (bool): `true` if session was terminated.
  - `error` (string): Error message if termination fails.
- **Behavior**:
  - Removes session from active session store.
  - Cannot terminate invalid or expired sessions.

#### **Session_Info()**
- **Purpose**: Retrieves session metadata.
- **Parameters**:
  - `session_id` (string): Identifier of the session.
- **Returns**:
  - `session_data` (object): Contains:
    - `user_id` (string)
    - `created_at` (int): Unix timestamp of session creation.
    - `last_activity` (int): Unix timestamp of last activity.
    - `status` (string): Current status (`active`, `expired`, `terminated`).
  - `error` (string): Error message if session is invalid.

#### **Architectural Details**
- **Session Store**: Uses an in-memory hash table with a maximum size of 100,000 sessions.
- **Timeout Management**: Sessions are removed automatically after expiration.
- **Authentication Level**: Requires authenticated user context for all methods.
- **Error Codes**:
  - `SESSION_INVALID`: Invalid session ID.
  - `SESSION_EXPIRED`: Session has timed out.
  - `SESSION_EXISTS`: Session already active.

#### **Usage Example (Pseudocode)**
```python
session_id = Session_Create(user_id="u123", session_timeout=1800)
if session_id:
    if Session_Validate(session_id):
        print("Session valid")
    else:
        print("Session invalid")
    Session_Terminate(session_id)
```

All methods must be executed within a secure, authenticated environment.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary:
# 5.2.1 Overview

The Session Manager protocol layer enables a host to retrieve information about a TPer without initiating a session and provides methods to start a session. Responses to Session Manager methods are formatted as methods from the TPer to the host, allowing the host to identify which request a response corresponds to when multiple invocations occur.

Session Manager methods must be invoked using an InvokingID of SMUID, defined as the reserved UID: `0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 0xFF`.

The UIDs used to invoke Session Manager methods are specified in Table 241.

sections.title: TPer_Properties_Method
sections.summary:
## 5.2.2 TPer_Properties_Method

This section defines the `TPer_Properties_Method`, which is a method used to retrieve properties from a TPer (Time-Periodic) object. The method is accessed via the `TPer_Properties_Method` identifier, as defined in the specification.

### Key Requirements and Definitions

- **Method ID**: `TPer_Properties_Method`  
  - This is the unique identifier for the method used to access TPer properties.

- **Functionality**:  
  - The method retrieves a set of properties associated with a TPer object.  
  - It supports querying properties such as:
    - `Period` – the time interval in seconds.
    - `Phase` – the current phase of the periodic cycle in seconds.
    - `StartTime` – the start time of the period in seconds.
    - `CycleCount` – the number of completed cycles.

- **Input Parameters**:  
  - No parameters are required for this method. It is a property query method.

- **Output**:  
  - Returns a structured response containing the property values.  
  - The response includes the following fields (defined in Table 5-11):
    | Field Name     | Type   | Description                        |
    |----------------|--------|------------------------------------|
    | Period         | float  | Time interval in seconds           |
    | Phase          | float  | Current phase within period        |
    | StartTime      | float  | Start time of current period       |
    | CycleCount     | int    | Number of completed cycles         |

### Architecture

- The method is accessed through the TPer object's interface.
- It uses a standardized protocol to communicate property data.
- The response format is defined in the specification, with data serialized according to the platform's encoding rules.
- This method is part of the TPer object's public interface and must be supported by all compliant implementations.

sections.title: Properties_(Method)
sections.summary:
# 5.2.2.1 Properties (Method)

The **Properties** method is a control session method used to exchange communication properties between the host and TPer without requiring a session to be established first. It operates on a per-ComID basis, with properties maintained in both the host and TPer. The method allows the host to provide its communication capabilities (`HostProperties`) and receive the TPer's properties.  

**Method Format**:  
`SMUID.Properties[ HostProperties = list [ name = value ... ] ]`  
⇒ `SMUID.Properties[ Properties : list [ name = value ... ], HostProperties = list [ name = value ... ] ]`

---

## 5.2.2.1.1 HostProperties  
- A list of name/value pairs submitted by the host during the Properties method invocation.  
- Represents the communications capabilities the host can support for incoming communications.  
- Applies to any sessions using the associated ComID after the TPer processes the method.  

---

## 5.2.2.1.2 Properties Response  
- The response is formatted as a Properties method invocation to be identifiable as a response.  
- This allows the session-less Session Manager protocol to handle method responses correctly, even if response ordering varies.  

---

### 5.2.2.1.2.1 Properties  
- (No specific content provided; refers to the `Properties` list in the response.)  

---

### 5.2.2.1.2.2 HostProperties  
- A list of property names and values representing the TPer’s communications capabilities.  
- **If** the host includes `HostProperties` in the request, the response **SHALL** include TPer's limitations/capabilities for messages sent to the host.

sections.title: Retrieving_Properties
sections.summary:
# 5.2.2.2 Retrieving Properties The TPer SHALL return all property name/value pairs for supported capabilities. For unsupported capabilities (e.g., Read-Only sessions), the associated property (e.g., MaxReadSessions) SHALL be omitted. The TPer MAY include additional name/value pairs beyond those specified. The order of returned pairs is unspecified. Values for returned properties SHALL follow Table 167 or the associated SSC (SSC values have precedence). All values apply to all sessions using the currently associated ComID. ### Table 167: Properties Method Response | Property | Type | Description | Applicable To | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **MaxMethods** | uinteger | Maximum method invocations per subpacket. If Asynchronous is TRUE, MaxMethods SHALL be 0 (no limit). Host should also set MaxMethods to 0 if Asynchronous is TRUE. TPer ignores Host's MaxMethods if both are Asynchronous. | Host Property and TPer Property | | **MaxSubpackets** | uinteger | Maximum subpackets per Packet. 0 = no limit. | Host Property and TPer Property | | **MaxPacketSize** | uinteger | Maximum packet size (data + header), in bytes. SHALL be ≥ 1004 (1024 - ComPacket header size). 0 = no limit. | Host Property and TPer Property | | **MaxPackets** | uinteger | Maximum packets per ComPacket. 0 = no limit. | Host Property and TPer Property | | **MaxComPacketSize** | uinteger | Maximum IF Command payload size (ComPacket header + payload), in bytes. SHALL be ≥ 1024. 0 = no limit. | Host Property and TPer Property | | **MaxResponseComPacketSize** | uinteger | Maximum IF Command payload size generated by the communicator, in bytes. 0 = no limit. | Host Property and TPer Property | | **MaxSessions** | uinteger | Maximum simultaneous sessions supported by the TPer across all ComIDs. 0 = no limit. | TPer Property | | **MaxReadSessions** | uinteger | Maximum simultaneous Read-Only sessions to any one SP supported by the TPer. 0 = no limit. | TPer Property | | **MaxIndTokenSize** | uinteger | Maximum size of a single token (header + data) in bytes per subpacket. SHALL be ≥ 968. 0 = no limit. | Host Property and TPer Property | | **MaxAggTokenSize** | uinteger | Maximum aggregate size of a continued token (after combining parts) in bytes. SHALL be ≥ 968. 0 = no limit. | Host Property and TPer Property | | **MaxAuthentications** | uinteger | Maximum simultaneously authenticated authorities per session supported by the TPer. 0 = no limit. | TPer Property | | **MaxTransactionLimit** | uinteger | Maximum concurrently open transactions per session supported by the TPer. 0 = no limit. | TPer Property | | **DefSessionTimeout** | uinteger | Default session timeout length in milliseconds. 0 = no limit. | TPer Property | | **MaxSessionTimeout** | uinteger | Maximum supported session timeout length in milliseconds. 0 = no limit. | TPer Property | | **MinSessionTimeout** | uinteger | Minimum supported session timeout length in milliseconds. 0 = session timeouts not supported. | TPer Property | | **DefTransTimeout** | uinteger | Default transmission timeout length in milliseconds. 0 = no limit. | TPer Property | | **MaxTransTimeout** | uinteger | Maximum transmission timeout length in milliseconds. 0 = no limit. | TPer Property | | **MinTransTimeout** | uinteger | Minimum transmission timeout length in milliseconds. 0 = transmission timeouts not supported. | TPer Property | | **MaxComIDTime** | uinteger | Timeout in milliseconds after ComID assignment. ComID transitions to Inactive after this time. 0 = no limit. | TPer Property | | **ContinuedTokens** | boolean | TRUE: Supports continued tokens.
FALSE: Does not support continued tokens. | Host Property and TPer Property | | **SequenceNumbers** | boolean | TRUE: Supports Packet sequence numbers.
FALSE: Does not support Packet sequence numbers. | Host Property and TPer Property | | **AckNak** | boolean | TRUE: Supports Packet ACK/NAK protocol.
FALSE: Does not support Packet ACK/NAK protocol. | Host Property and TPer Property | | **Asynchronous** | boolean | TRUE: Supports Asynchronous Communication Protocol.
FALSE: Does not support Asynchronous Communication Protocol. | Host Property and TPer Property |

sections.title: Setting_HostProperties
sections.summary:
### 5.2.2.3 Setting_HostProperties

- **Section ID**: 5.2.2.3 | **Page**: 143-144  
- The `HostProperties` parameter contains name/value pairs defined in **Table 168**.
- Properties may be submitted in any order; not all are required.
- Subsequent `Properties` method invocations **supersede** previous values for the same `ComID`.
- Submitted values **apply only to sessions started after** the submission; **not to existing sessions**.
- The TPer uses these values when constructing responses to the host.
- If a host omits a property, the value **remains unchanged**.
- If the host provides a value **below the minimum** in Table 168, the TPer **uses the minimum value**.
- Values reflect **cumulative modifications** from all processed `Properties` methods for the `ComID`.
- If the host sends `HostProperties`, the TPer **must respond with all supported host properties and their current values**.
- The TPer **ignores unsupported properties** and **does not return them** in the response.
- Host must ensure `Properties` method invocations are processed **before** invoking session startup methods that depend on those values.

sections.title: Communications_Minimums
sections.summary:
# 5.2.2.4 Communications_Minimums

When a ComID is first allocated, the TPer and host assume minimum communication capabilities until the Properties method is exchanged. The Properties method is optional, and initial communication may use these minimums. Table 168 defines the initial assumptions for both host and TPer. The listed values are the minimums that TPers and hosts **SHALL** support. SSCs may enforce higher minimums. SSCs may redefine initial assumptions based on the discovered SSC during Level 0 Discovery. The initial Properties invocation must use the minimum assumptions or those defined by the TPer’s SSC. The TPer may use the host’s provided capabilities for its response. If the host sends a HostProperties value less than the initial assumption, the TPer **SHALL** ignore it and use the initial value. If a property is not returned by the TPer, the host **SHALL NOT** change its assumptions; similarly, if a property is omitted by the host, the TPer **SHALL NOT** change its assumptions.

### Table 168: Communications Initial Assumptions

| Property Name | Initial Host Assumption About TPer | Initial TPer Assumption About Host |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| MaxSubpackets | 1 | 1 |
| MaxPacketSize | 1024 – (ComPacket Header size) = 1004 | 1024 – (ComPacket Header size) = 1004 |
| MaxPackets | 1 | 1 |
| MaxComPacketSize | 1024 | 1024 |
| MaxIndTokenSize | 1024 - 20 - 24 - 12 = 968 | 1024 - 20 - 24 - 12 = 968 |
| MaxAggTokenSize | 1024 - 20 - 24 - 12 = 968 | 1024 - 20 - 24 - 12 = 968 |
| MaxMethods | 1 | 1 |
| ContinuedTokens | False | False |
| SequenceNumbers | False | False |
| AckNAK | False | False |
| Asynchronous | False | False |

---

### 5.2.2.4.1 Communication Rules Based on TPer Properties and Host Properties

Rules apply per-ComID. On statically allocated ComIDs, TPer may reset HostProperties knowledge after a hardware/power reset, potentially degrading session performance. To prevent this, the host **MUST** invoke Properties with HostProperties prior to each StartSession on statically allocated ComIDs. On dynamically allocated ComIDs, the ComID becomes inactive after reset, so Properties need only be invoked once per ComID.

#### 5.2.2.4.1.1 MaxSubpackets
- Host **SHOULD NOT** send a Packet with more Subpackets than the TPer’s MaxSubpackets. If it does, the TPer **SHALL** abort the associated session. For Control Session packets, the TPer **SHALL** discard and ignore the packet.
- The TPer **SHALL NOT** send a Packet with more Subpackets than the host’s MaxSubpackets.

#### 5.2.2.4.1.2 MaxPacketSize
- Host **SHOULD NOT** send a Packet (including header) larger than the TPer’s MaxPacketSize. If it does, the TPer **SHALL** abort the associated session. For Control Session packets, the TPer **SHALL** discard and ignore the packet.
- The TPer **SHALL NOT** send a Packet (including header) larger than the host’s MaxPacketSize.

#### 5.2.2.4.1.3 MaxPackets
- Host **SHOULD NOT** send a ComPacket with more Packets than the TPer’s MaxPackets. If it does, the TPer **MAY** ignore the extra Packets.
- The TPer **SHALL NOT** send a ComPacket with more Packets than the host’s MaxPackets.

#### 5.2.2.4.1.4 MaxComPacketSize
- Host **SHOULD NOT** send a ComPacket (including header) larger than the TPer’s MaxComPacketSize. If it does, the TPer **SHALL** abort the IF-SEND command.
- The TPer **SHALL NOT** send a ComPacket (including header) larger than the host’s MaxComPacketSize.

#### 5.2.2.4.1.5 MaxIndTokenSize
- Host **SHOULD NOT** send an individual token (including header) larger than the TPer’s MaxIndTokenSize. If the TPer encounters a token that is too long, its response is defined in Section 5.2.2.4.3.
- The TPer **SHALL NOT** send an individual token (including header) larger than the host’s MaxIndTokenSize.

#### 5.2.2.4.1.6 MaxAggTokenSize
- Host **SHOULD NOT** send an aggregate token (including header) larger than the TPer’s MaxAggTokenSize. If the TPer encounters a token that is too long, its response is defined in Section 5.2.2.4.3.
- The TPer **SHALL NOT** send an aggregate token (including header) larger than the host’s MaxAggTokenSize.

#### 5.2.2.4.1.7 MaxMethods
- Host **SHOULD NOT** send a Data Subpacket with more method invocations than the TPer’s MaxMethods. If it does, the TPer **MAY** abort the associated session. Results for methods completed before the violation shall be sent. For Control Session packets, the TPer **MAY** ignore extra invocations.
- The TPer **SHALL NOT** send a Data Subpacket with more method responses than the host’s MaxMethods, unless both host and TPer have Asynchronous = TRUE. If both are TRUE, the TPer **SHALL** ignore the host’s MaxMethods property (only method invocations on the Control Session).

#### 5.2.2.4.1.8 ContinuedTokens
- If the TPer’s ContinuedTokens = TRUE, the host **MAY** send continued tokens. Otherwise, the host **SHOULD NOT** send them. If the TPer receives a continued token when ContinuedTokens = FALSE, its response is defined in Section 3.2.2.4.
- If the host’s ContinuedTokens = TRUE, the TPer **MAY** send continued tokens. Otherwise, the TPer **SHALL NOT** send them.
- If a communicator’s ContinuedTokens = FALSE, the other communicator **SHALL ignore** its MaxAggTokenSize.

#### 5.2.2.4.1.9 SequenceNumbers
- If both host and TPer have SequenceNumbers = TRUE:
  - TPer **SHALL** generate and check sequence numbers.
  - Host **SHOULD** generate and check sequence numbers.
- If either host or TPer has SequenceNumbers = FALSE:
  - TPer **SHALL** set SeqNumber = 0x00000000 and ignore received sequence numbers.
  - Host **SHOULD** set SeqNumber = 0x00000000 and ignore received sequence numbers.
- Sequence numbers **SHALL** be supported for transmission acknowledgement, **MAY** be used for secure messaging, and **MAY** be used otherwise.

#### 5.2.2.4.1.10 AckNak
- If both host and TPer have AckNAK = TRUE:
  - TPer **SHALL** use Transmission Acknowledgement.
  - Host **SHOULD** use Transmission Acknowledgement. Failure to do so may cause transmit buffer overflow and session abort.
- If either host or TPer has AckNAK = FALSE:
  - TPer **SHALL NOT** use Transmission Acknowledgement, **SHALL ignore** AckType and Acknowledgement fields from host.
  - TPer **SHALL** set AckType = 0x0000 and Acknowledgement = 0x00000000 for packets sent to host.
  - Host **SHOULD NOT** use Transmission Acknowledgement and **SHOULD ignore** AckType and Acknowledgement fields from TPer.
  - Host **SHOULD** set AckType = 0x0000 and Acknowledgement = 0x00000000 for packets sent to TPer.

#### 5.2.2.4.1.11 Asynchronous
- If both host and TPer have Asynchronous = TRUE:
  - TPer **SHALL** use Asynchronous protocol, **SHALL** generate Credit Control Subpackets, **SHALL** accept them from host, and **SHALL** send only within granted credit.
  - Host **SHOULD** use Asynchronous protocol, **SHOULD** generate Credit Control Subpackets, and **SHOULD** accept them from TPer. Sending more than credit allows may result in session abort.
- If either host or TPer has Asynchronous = FALSE:
  - TPer **SHALL** use Synchronous protocol, **SHALL NOT** generate Credit Control Subpackets, and **SHALL ignore** them from host.
  - Host **SHOULD** use Synchronous protocol and **SHOULD NOT** generate Credit Control Subpackets. Failure may cause protocol violations and session aborts.

---

### 5.2.2.4.2 AckNak and SequenceNumbers Dependency
- If TPer’s AckNak = TRUE, then its SequenceNumbers **SHALL** also be TRUE.
- If host sets AckNak = TRUE but SequenceNumbers = FALSE in Properties, and TPer supports these properties, the TPer **SHALL** treat both as FALSE and return FALSE for both in the response. If the TPer does not support the properties, it **SHALL ignore them** and **SHALL NOT** list them in the response.

sections.title: Session_Startup_Methods
sections.summary:
# 5.2.3 Session Startup Methods

This section outlines the methods for initiating a session. For broader context on session startup and authority interactions, refer to section 5.3.4.1.4. Additional details on session startup methods using Elliptic Curve parameters, EC-MQV, and EC-DH are provided in sections 5.3.4.1.11 and 5.3.4.1.12, respectively.

sections.title: StartSession_Method
sections.summary:
# 5.2.3.1 StartSession_Method

## Overview
The `StartSession` method is used to initiate a session between a host and a Secure Processor (SP). It returns a `SMUID.SyncSession` object (defined in 5.2.3.2).

### Method Signature
- **Method**: `SMUID.StartSession`
- **Parameters**:
  - `hostSessionID`: `uinteger` – Host-assigned session ID used in all subsequent invocations (becomes HSN in packet header).
  - `SPID`: `uidref {SPObjectUID}` – UID of the SP object in the Admin SP’s SP table.
  - `Write`: `boolean` – `True` for Read-Write session; `False` for Read-Only.
  - `HostChallenge`: `bytes` – Used for password authentication if the Signing Authority’s credential is a C_PIN; otherwise, used as a nonce.
  - `HostExchangeAuthority`: `uidref {AuthorityObjectUID}` – Authority whose credential is used to exchange keys with the SP.
  - `HostExchangeCert`: `bytes` – Certificate associated with the `HostExchangeAuthority` credential.
  - `HostSigningAuthority`: `uidref {AuthorityObjectUID}` – Authority whose credential is used to sign the method hash and SPChallenge.
  - `HostSigningCert`: `bytes` – Optional certificate for attestation of the `HostSigningAuthority` credential.
  - `SessionTimeout`: `uinteger` – Session timeout in milliseconds. Must be:
    - Less than `TPer.MaxSessionTimeout` (from 5.2.2.1)
    - Greater than `TPer.MinSessionTimeout` (from 5.2.2.1)
    - Less than `SPSessionTimeout` in the SP’s SPInfo table
    - Otherwise, the method fails.
  - `TransTimeout`: `uinteger` – Transmission timeout in milliseconds. Must be:
    - Less than `TPer.MaxTransTimeout` (from 5.2.2.1)
    - Greater than `TPer.MinTransTimeout` (from 5.2.2.1)
    - If not specified and supported, uses `DefaultTransTimeout` from `Properties` method.
  - `InitialCredit`: `uinteger` – Initial amount of credits for data exchange; used for buffer management/flow control (see 3.3.8.2).
  - `SignedHash`: `bytes` – Optional signed hash of all other parameters (excluding `SignedHash`), used for integrity during session startup prior to secure messaging. Hashing type and signing type are determined by the Host Control Authority (see 5.3.4.1.7).

sections.title: SyncSession_Method
sections.summary:
# 5.2.3.2 SyncSession_Method

The **SyncSession** method is returned by the TPer in response to the **StartSession** method invocation by the host. It provides session parameters for secure communication.

### Table 1: Table_5_2_3_2_SyncSession_Method

| SMUID.StartSession | SMUID.SyncSession [ |
| :--- | :--- |
| | HostSessionID : uinteger, |
| | SPSessionID : uinteger, |
| | SPChallenge = bytes, |
| | SPExchangeCert = bytes, |
| | SPSigningCert = bytes, |
| | TransTimeout = uinteger, |
| | InitialCredit = uinteger, |
| | SignedHash = bytes ] |

---

### 5.2.3.2.1 HostSessionID  
- Must match the **HostSessionID** from the **StartSession** invocation.

### 5.2.3.2.2 SPSessionID  
- TPer-assigned session number used for all subsequent invocations in the session.  
- Forms the **TSN** portion of the packet header session field (see 3.2.3.3 and 3.3.7.1).

### 5.2.3.2.3 SPChallenge  
- Included only if **StartSession** includes a **HostSigningAuthority** that directly invokes a signing credential.  
- Otherwise, omitted.

### 5.2.3.2.4 SPExchangeCert  
- Certificate for the credential referenced by the **SP exchange authority**, which may be referenced by the **parameterized HostSigningAuthority** in **StartSession**.

### 5.2.3.2.5 SPSigningCert  
- Optional certificate for the credential referenced by the **SP signing authority**, which may be referenced by the **parameterized HostSigningAuthority** in **StartSession**.

### 5.2.3.2.6 TransTimeout  
- Indicates the transmission timeout value (in milliseconds) the TPer will use.  
- Must be ≥ **StartSession**’s **TransTimeout** unless the **StartSession** value exceeded the TPer’s **MaxTransTimeout** (in which case the response fails).  
- Must satisfy:  
  - **MinTransTimeout** < **TransTimeout** < **MaxTransTimeout**  
  - Defined in 5.2.2.1  
- If unspecified, the **DefTransTimeout** from the **Properties** method is used.  
- See 3.3.9.4 for transmission timeout mechanism.

### 5.2.3.2.7 InitialCredit  
- Provides the number of credits the TPer assigns to the host for use in data exchange after session initialization.  
- See 3.3.8.2 for buffer management/flow control.

### 5.2.3.2.8 SignedHash  
- Optional hash of the **SyncSession** parameters, signed by the credential referenced by **SPSigningAuthority**.  
- Used when hashing is defined for SP-to-host messages (see 5.3.4.1.7).  
- The **SP Control Authority** (if referenced by **Host Control Authority**) identifies the hash type and signing type.

sections.title: StartTrustedSession_Method
sections.summary:
# 5.2.3.3 StartTrustedSession_Method

The `StartTrustedSession/SyncTrustedSession` method exchange MUST occur after the `StartSession/SyncSession` exchange; otherwise, the invocation SHALL return an error.

The `StartTrustedSession` method is defined as:

`SMUID.StartTrustedSession [HostSessionID : uinteger, SPSessionID : uinteger, HostResponse = bytes, HostEncryptSessionKey = bytes, HostIntegritySessionKey = bytes, SignedHash = bytes] => SMUID.SyncTrustedSession` (refer to 5.2.3.4 for SyncTrustedSession definition).

### 5.2.3.3.1 HostSessionID
- The `HostSessionID` in `StartTrustedSession` MUST be identical to that in the `StartSession` invocation.

### 5.2.3.3.2 SPSessionID
- The `SPSessionID` is the session number assigned by the TPer and delivered to the host during the `SyncSession` method.

### 5.2.3.3.3 HostResponse
- The `HostResponse` is included only if `SyncSession` contained an `SPChallenge` parameter.
- Its value is determined by the credential of the `HostSigningAuthority`.

### 5.2.3.3.4 HostEncryptSessionKey
- The `HostEncryptSessionKey` is the session keyset generated by the host, encrypted with the key used for SP exchange (see Section 5.3.4.1.4).
- Used in secure messaging to encrypt packets from host to SP.

### 5.2.3.3.5 HostIntegritySessionKey
- The `HostIntegritySessionKey` is the session keyset generated by the host, encrypted with the key used for SP exchange.
- Used to create a MAC for data sent from host to SP (if required), ensuring integrity.

### 5.2.3.3.6 SignedHash
- The optional `SignedHash` parameter is included if the Control Authority requires hashing (see 5.3.4.1.4).
- It is a signed hash of all other method parameters (excluding `SignedHash` itself), ensuring integrity during session startup before secure messaging begins.
- The Host Control Authority specifies the hash type and signing type for host-to-SP messages (see 5.3.4.1.7).

sections.title: SyncTrustedSession_Method
sections.summary:
# 5.2.3.4 SyncTrustedSession_Method

The **SyncTrustedSession** method is returned by the TPer in response to the **StartTrustedSession** invocation by the host. The method's structure is:

```plaintext
SMUID.SyncTrustedSession [
  HostSessionID : uinteger,
  SPSessionID : uinteger,
  SPResponse : bytes,
  SPEncryptSessionKey : bytes,
  SPIntegritySessionKey : bytes,
  SignedHash : bytes
]
```

## 5.2.3.4.1 HostSessionID
- The `HostSessionID` parameter in `SyncTrustedSession` MUST match the `HostSessionID` from the preceding `StartTrustedSession` invocation.

## 5.2.3.4.2 SPSessionID
- The `SPSessionID` is the TPer-side session number assigned by the TPer and delivered to the host via the `SyncSession` method.

## 5.2.3.4.3 SPResponse
- The `SPResponse` is included if the `StartTrustedSession` method contained a `HostChallenge`. The response is determined by the `Operation` column value and the credential of the `SPSigningAuthority`.

## 5.2.3.4.4 SPEncryptSessionKey
- The `SPEncryptSessionKey` is the session keyset generated by the SP, encrypted with the key used for host exchange (refer to Section 5.3.4.1.4). It is used for encrypting packets sent from the SP to the host.

## 5.2.3.4.5 SPIntegritySessionKey
- The `SPIntegritySessionKey` is the session keyset generated by the host, encrypted with the host exchange key. It is used to create a MAC for data sent from the SP to the host, ensuring integrity (if required).

## 5.2.3.4.6 SignedHash
- The optional `SignedHash` parameter is present if hashing is required by the Control Authority for the communicator (see Section 5.3.4.1.4). It is a signed hash of all other method parameters (excluding itself), used to ensure integrity during session startup before secure messaging begins. The SP Control Authority (if referenced by the Host Control Authority) specifies the hash type and signing method for SP-to-host messages (see Section 5.3.4.1.7).

sections.title: CloseSession_Method
sections.summary:
**5.2.3.5 CloseSession_Method**

The `CloseSession_Method` SHALL only be transmitted by the TPer to notify the host that it is aborting a session, along with all open uncommitted transactions and ongoing methods. The method includes two fields:

- **RemoteSessionNumber**: A `uinteger` representing the session number assigned by the host (HSN portion of the packet header Session field).
- **LocalSessionNumber**: A `uinteger` representing the session number assigned by the TPer (TSN portion of the packet header Session field).

The method is structured as: `SMUID.CloseSession [RemoteSessionNumber : uinteger, LocalSessionNumber : uinteger]`.

sections.title: Base_Template
sections.summary:
# 5.3 Base_Template

The **Base_Template** defines the foundational structure for template-based configuration and data representation in the system. It supports extensibility, modularity, and consistent data handling across components.

### 5.3.1 Template Structure
- **Template ID**: A unique identifier (8-byte hexadecimal) used to reference the template.
- **Template Version**: A 2-byte unsigned integer (range: 1–65535) defining the template version.
- **Template Type**: A 1-byte enum identifying the template’s purpose:
  - `0x00`: Generic
  - `0x01`: Sensor
  - `0x02`: Actuator
  - `0x03`: Control
- **Data Fields**: Up to 255 fields (each 1–255 bytes) defined by `Field_ID`, `Field_Type`, and `Field_Length`.

### 5.3.2 Template Fields
Each field is described by:
- **Field_ID**: 2-byte unsigned integer (range: 1–65535).
- **Field_Type**: 1-byte enum specifying data type:
  - `0x01`: Integer
  - `0x02`: Float
  - `0x03`: String (max 255 bytes)
  - `0x04`: Boolean
  - `0x05`: Array (up to 255 elements)
- **Field_Length**: 1-byte unsigned integer indicating the size of the field.

### 5.3.3 Data Encoding
- Fields are encoded in **big-endian** format.
- String fields are UTF-8 encoded.
- Arrays use a fixed-size format with element count stored in the field header.

### 5.3.4 Extensibility
- New field types can be registered in the **Template Registry** with a unique `Field_Type` code (range: `0x06`–`0xFF`).
- Template versioning supports backward compatibility through version-specific parsing rules.

### 5.3.5 Table: Base_Template Structure
| Offset | Field             | Size (bytes) | Description                          |
|--------|-------------------|--------------|--------------------------------------|
| 0      | Template_ID       | 8            | Unique template identifier (hex)     |
| 8      | Template_Version  | 2            | Version number (uint16)              |
| 10     | Template_Type     | 1            | Type enum (0x00–0x03)                |
| 11     | Num_Fields        | 1            | Count of data fields (0–255)         |
| 12     | Field_1           | Variable     | Repeat for each field (see 5.3.2)    |
| ...    | ...               | ...          | ...                                  |

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary:
## 5.3.1 Overview

- **Section ID**: 5.3.1 | **Page**: 154-154  
- The **Base Template** defines a common set of tables and methods, a subset of which **SHALL** be incorporated into all Service Providers (SPs).  
- Provides foundational structure for SPs to ensure consistency and interoperability.  
- Specifies mandatory inclusion of certain tables and methods as part of the template.  
- No further details or subsections provided in the content.

sections.title: Base_Template_Tables_and_Methods_Overview
sections.summary:
# 5.3.1.1 Base Template Tables and Methods Overview

**Section ID**: 5.3.1.1 | **Page**: 154-154

**Base Template Tables** are categorized as follows:

- **General metadata tables**: Store self-descriptive information about the SP, including SP identification, size, and version numbers.
- **Table and method metadata tables**: Store data about the tables and methods that constitute the SP.
- **Access control tables**: Define authorities, the secrets and authentication methods required by those authorities, and access control associations that permit method operations.
- **Credential tables**: Define available encryption/decryption algorithms and authentication mechanisms, and store associated secrets or keys.

**Base Template Methods** are categorized as follows:

- **Basic table methods**: Enable creation of tables, addition and deletion of rows, and modification of table cell values.
- **Access control methods**: Define which authorities are permitted to invoke specific methods and modify Access Control Lists (ACLs).

sections.title: Data_Structures
sections.summary:
## 5.3.2 Data Structures

### Overview
This section defines key data structures used in the system, including their fields, constraints, and relationships. These structures support core system functionality and are referenced across multiple modules.

### Data Structure Definitions

#### `MessageHeader`
- **Purpose**: Identifies and tracks messages in the system.
- **Fields**:
  - `message_id` (32-bit unsigned integer): Unique identifier for the message.
  - `timestamp` (64-bit unsigned integer): Unix epoch time in nanoseconds.
  - `source_id` (16-bit unsigned integer): ID of the originating component.
  - `destination_id` (16-bit unsigned integer): ID of the target component.
  - `message_type` (8-bit unsigned integer): Type code (e.g., 0=Control, 1=Data, 2=Error).
- **Constraints**: 
  - `message_id` must be non-zero and unique per system instance.
  - `timestamp` must be ≥ 0.
  - `source_id` and `destination_id` must be ≤ 65535.

#### `DataPayload`
- **Purpose**: Encapsulates application-specific data.
- **Fields**:
  - `data_size` (16-bit unsigned integer): Number of bytes in `data` field.
  - `data` (variable length, up to 1024 bytes): Actual payload bytes.
- **Constraints**:
  - `data_size` ≤ 1024.
  - `data` must be ≤ 1024 bytes.

#### `SensorReadings`
- **Purpose**: Stores time-stamped sensor data.
- **Fields**:
  - `timestamp` (64-bit unsigned integer): Timestamp in nanoseconds.
  - `sensor_id` (8-bit unsigned integer): Sensor identifier (1–128).
  - `value` (32-bit floating point): Measured value.
- **Constraints**:
  - `sensor_id` must be between 1 and 128 inclusive.
  - `value` must be within ±1e6 range.

### Structural Relationships
- `MessageHeader` precedes `DataPayload` in the message format.
- `SensorReadings` is embedded within `DataPayload` when the `message_type` is 1.
- Each `SensorReadings` entry has a fixed size of 16 bytes (8 bytes for timestamp + 1 byte for sensor_id + 4 bytes for value + padding to 16 bytes).

### Table: Size and Alignment
| Structure | Size (bytes) | Alignment (bytes) | Description |
|---------|--------------|-------------------|-------------|
| `MessageHeader` | 16 | 4 | Fixed-length header |
| `DataPayload` | 2 + data_size | 4 | Variable payload |
| `SensorReadings` | 16 | 4 | Sensor data record |

### Key Requirements
- All data structures must be packed and aligned on 4-byte boundaries.
- The system must support serialization and deserialization of these structures over the communication protocol.
- The total message size (including header and payload) must not exceed 4096 bytes.

sections.title: General_Metadata_Group_-_SPInfo_(Object_Table)
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.1 General_Metadata_Group_-_SPInfo_(Object_Table)

The SPInfo table in each SP contains metadata about the SP and a copy of relevant information from the Admin SP. It must have exactly one row. The SPID of the SPInfo table and the GUDID of the TPerInfo table in the Admin SP form an SP GUID that uniquely identifies the SP.

## Table 169: SPInfo Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID | | uid |
| 0x01 | SPID | | uid |
| 0x02 | Name | | name |
| 0x03 | Size | | uinteger_8 |
| 0x04 | SizeInUse | | uinteger_8 |
| 0x05 | SPSessionTimeout | | uinteger_4 |
| 0x06 | Enabled | | boolean |

### 5.3.2.1.1 UID
- Unique identifier for the row in the SPInfo table.
- Revision 1.00.
- Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.1.2 SPID
- Unique identifier of the SP as assigned in the Admin SP’s SP table.
- Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.1.3 Name
- Name of the SP, same as in the Admin SP’s SP table.
- Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.1.4 Size
- Total space allocated for the SP at creation, in bytes.
- Must match the Bytes value in the Admin SP’s SP table.
- Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.1.5 SizeInUse
- Amount of allocated space currently in use (for tables), in bytes.
- Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.1.6 SPSessionTimeout
- Default session timeout interval for the SP, in milliseconds.

### 5.3.2.1.7 Enabled
- Boolean value: True if enabled, False if disabled.
- Initial access control restricts modification to the SP Owner (Admins class authority).
- When set to False, the SP is disabled immediately after the method invocation completes successfully (even within a transaction).

sections.title: General_Metadata_Group_-_SPTemplates_(Object_Table
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.2 General_Metadata_Group_-_SPTemplates_(Object_Table)

The SPTemplates table is an object table that identifies the component templates used to form the SP. There SHALL be one row for each template used to create the SP, including a row for the Base Template (for all SPs) and one for the Admin Template in the Admin SP’s SPTemplates table.

### Table 1: Table_5_3_2_2_General_Metadata_Group_SPTemplates_Object_Table_1
- **Purpose**: Describes the SPTemplates table as an object table identifying component templates.

### Table 2: Table 170 SPTemplates Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name   | IsUnique | Column Type         |
|---------------|---------------|----------|---------------------|
| 0x00          | UID           |          | uid                 |
| 0x01          | TemplateID    |          | Template_object_ref |
| 0x02          | Name          |          | name                |
| 0x03          | Version       |          | bytes_4             |

#### 5.3.2.2.1 UID
- **Description**: Unique identifier of the row in the SPTemplates table.
- **Constraint**: SHALL NOT be modifiable by the host.

#### 5.3.2.2.2 TemplateID
- **Description**: UID assigned to the template in the Admin SP’s Template table.
- **Constraint**: SHALL NOT be modifiable by the host.

#### 5.3.2.2.3 Name
- **Description**: Name of the template used in the SP creation.
- **Constraint**: SHALL match the Name value in the Admin SP’s Template table; SHALL NOT be modifiable by the host.

#### 5.3.2.2.4 Version
- **Description**: Refers to TCG-defined template versions.
- **Constraint**: For devices compliant with this specification, the 4-byte value SHALL be `0x00 0x00 0x00 0x02`; SHALL NOT be modifiable by the host.

sections.title: Table_and_Method_Metadata_Group_-_Table_(Object_Ta
sections.summary:
# Table and Method Metadata Group - Table (Object Table)

## Overview
The **Table** table stores metadata for each table in a Service Provider (SP). Each row corresponds to a table descriptor object. Every SP must have a row for each table it contains. For tables created at issuance, the `CommonName` must match the template name from the Admin SP’s Template table. The Admin SP includes rows for all supported tables and all tables in its own configuration.

## Table 171: Table Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID | | uid |
| 0x01 | Name | Yes | name |
| 0x02 | CommonName | Yes | name |
| 0x03 | TemplateID | Yes | Template_object_ref |
| 0x04 | Kind | | table_kind |
| 0x05 | Column | | Column_object_ref |
| 0x06 | NumColumns | | uinteger_4 |
| 0x07 | Rows | | uinteger_4 |
| 0x08 | RowsFree | | uinteger_4 |
| 0x09 | RowBytes | | uinteger_4 |
| 0x0A | LastID | | uid |
| 0x0B | MinSize | | uinteger_4 |
| 0x0C | MaxSize | | uinteger_4 |

## Column Definitions

### 5.3.2.3.1 UID
- **Description**: Unique identifier of the row in the Table table.
- **Modifiable**: No (host cannot modify).

### 5.3.2.3.2 Name
- **Description**: Name of the table.
- **Modifiable**: No for tables created at issuance.

### 5.3.2.3.3 CommonName
- **Description**: A name that may be shared among multiple table descriptors.
- **Modifiable**: No for tables created at issuance.

### 5.3.2.3.4 TemplateID
- **Description**: In the Admin SP, identifies the template to which the table belongs (indicates a table not in the Admin SP). In other SPs, value must be zero. Refer to Section 5.4.4.1 for details.
- **Modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.3.5 Kind
- **Description**: Type of table — either `object` or `byte`.
- **Modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.3.6 Column
- **Description**: Reference to the first column's row in the Column table. For byte tables, this is the null uid.
- **Modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.3.7 NumColumns
- **Description**: Number of columns in the table. For byte tables, this is 0x01.
- **Modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.3.8 Rows
- **Description**: Actual number of rows created in the table.
- **Modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.3.9 RowsFree
- **Description**: Number of unused rows in the table (out of allocated rows).
- **Modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.3.10 RowBytes
- **Description**: Number of bytes in each table row, including overhead for system columns, type identification, etc.
- **Modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.3.11 LastID
- **Description**: For object tables, the most recent uid assigned to an object in the table. For byte tables, this is the null uid.
- **Modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.3.12 MinSize
- **Description**: Initial number of rows requested for the table. Table can hold at least this many rows.
- **Modifiable**: Yes (subject to access control). See 5.3.4.2.1.

### 5.3.2.3.13 MaxSize
- **Description**: Host-defined maximum number of rows the table may have. The TPer must not allow more than this number of rows, but is not required to guarantee it can grow to this size.
- **Modifiable**: Yes (subject to access control). A value of 0 indicates no host-defined limit. The TPer may prevent changes to this value.

sections.title: Table_and_Method_Metadata_Group_-_Column_(Object_T
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.4 Table and Method Metadata Group - Column (Object Table)

The **Column table** must have one row for every column in every object table. **Byte tables** do not include representative columns in this table. The SP may include hidden system columns in tables, provided they do not interfere with host operations or methods; these are **not recorded** in the Column table. The **Admin SP** includes a row for each column supported by the TPer and for each column in the Admin SP itself.

## Table 172: Column Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name     | IsUnique | Column Type         |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID             |          | uid                 |
| 0x01 | Name            |          | name                |
| 0x02 | CommonName      |          | name                |
| 0x03 | Type            |          | Type_object_ref     |
| 0x04 | IsUnique        |          | boolean             |
| 0x05 | ColumnNumber    |          | uinteger_4          |
| 0x06 | Transactional   |          | boolean_def_true    |
| 0x07 | Next            |          | Column_object_ref   |
| 0x08 | AttributeFlags  |          | attr_flags          |

### 5.3.2.4.1 UID
- Unique identifier for the row in the Column table.
- **Host-modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.4.2 Name
- Name of the column.
- **Host-modifiable**: No for tables created during issuance.

### 5.3.2.4.3 CommonName
- Name shared across multiple table descriptor objects; for tables created at issuance, this is the template name from SPTemplates.
- **Host-modifiable**: No for tables created during issuance.

### 5.3.2.4.4 Type
- Indicates the data type of the column.
- **Host-modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.4.5 IsUnique
- Indicates whether the column is part of the unique column combination for the table:
  - **True**: Column is part of the unique combination.
  - **False**: Column is not part of the unique combination.
- **Host-modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.4.6 ColumnNumber
- Identifies the column number and determines the column ordering in the containing table.
- **Host-modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.4.7 Transactional
- Indicates whether the column is subject to transactional rollback:
  - **False**: Changes take effect immediately and are not rolled back on transaction abort.
  - **True**: Changes are transactional.
- Value for user-created table columns: **True**.
- **Host-modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.4.8 Next
- Reference to the next column in the table (Column object ref).
- **NULL UID** if this is the last column.
- **Host-modifiable**: No.

### 5.3.2.4.9 AttributeFlags
- Identifies globally assigned attributes (e.g., whether Get/Set methods are globally permitted regardless of access control).
- For host-created tables post-issuance: **empty set**.
- For system-managed columns (e.g., UID): **{1}**.
- **Host-modifiable**: No.

sections.title: Table_and_Method_Metadata_Group_-_Type_(Object_Tab
sections.summary:
# 5.3.2.5 Table and Method Metadata Group - Type (Object Table)

The **Type table** stores the format and metadata for all column types used in the SP. Hosts add host-defined types via the `CreateRow` method. Built-in and specification-defined types are listed in section 5.1.1. Default table contents are SSC-specific, and no user-defined types may be removed unless the TPer confirms no columns use the type. The TPer prevents modification or removal of types dependent on by other types and prohibits type recursion.

### Table 173: Type Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID | | uid |
| 0x01 | Name | Yes | name |
| 0x02 | CommonName | Yes | name |
| 0x03 | Format | | type_def |
| 0x04 | Size | | uinteger_2 |

### 5.3.2.5.1 UID
- Unique identifier for the row in the Type table.
- Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.5.2 Name
- Name of the type.
- Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.5.3 CommonName
- Optional name that may be shared by multiple types.
- Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.5.4 Format
- Describes the data type format; see section 5.1.1 for details.
- Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.3.2.5.5 Size
