sections.title: Description
sections.summary:
## 5.3.4 Description

This section describes the functionality and configuration of the **Spare Channel** feature, which enables automatic channel switching in case of a failure of the primary channel.

### Key Requirements:
- The Spare Channel must be activated automatically when the primary channel is lost.
- The system must ensure seamless transition to the spare channel without data loss.
- The spare channel must be configured with a priority level (High, Medium, Low).
- The primary channel must be monitored continuously for availability.
- If the primary channel fails, the spare channel must be selected within 100 ms.

### Definitions:
- **Primary Channel**: The main communication channel in use.
- **Spare Channel**: A backup channel activated when the primary channel fails.
- **Failover Time**: The time required to switch from the primary to the spare channel (must be ≤ 100 ms).

### Architectural Details:
- The failover mechanism is implemented in the **Channel Controller** component.
- The **Synchronization Module** ensures that both primary and spare channels are synchronized before failover.
- The **Monitor Module** continuously checks the health status of the primary channel at 100 ms intervals.

### Configuration Table:
| Parameter            | Value               |
|----------------------|---------------------|
| Failover Time        | ≤ 100 ms            |
| Polling Interval     | 100 ms              |
| Channel Priority     | High, Medium, Low   |
| Synchronization Period | 1 second           |

> **Section ID**: 5.3.4 | **Page**: 210-210

sections.title: Authentication
sections.summary:
# 5.3.4.1 Authentication

## Credential Tables
- Credential tables are extensible structures for authentication mechanisms and key stores.
- Each table represents a mechanism or key store type; each row represents an authentication or key using that mechanism.
- Supported credential tables must be listed in the CryptoSuite table in the Admin SP.
- Shaded (marked) columns in credential tables may be hidden; the mechanism used is discoverable via the SecretProtect table.

## 5.3.4.1.1.1 GenKey on C_PIN Objects
- If the `CharSet` column is a NULL UID reference, the default character set for `GenKey` is ASCII printable characters.
- Default `CharSet` value is zeroes.
- Non-zero `CharSet` value must be a UID to a byte table defining the character set for `GenKey`.
- A `CharSet` value of `0x00 0x00 0x00 0x0B 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01` indicates no restriction (all bytes are legal).
- The TPer does not enforce the character set when the host sets the PIN via `Set`.

## 5.3.4.1.1.2 Authentication Attempt Limits with C_PIN Objects
- Authentication attempt limits are managed using `Tries` and `TryLimit` columns in the C_PIN table.
- Default `Tries` is 0 when a new C_PIN object is created.
- `Tries` increments on each failed authentication (including implicit authentication during session startup).
- If `Tries` equals `TryLimit` (and `TryLimit` ≠ 0), further authentication attempts fail until `Tries` is reset.
- `Tries` resets to 0 after successful `Authenticate`, `Set`, `GenKey`, or `SetPackage` methods.
- `Tries` resets to 0 after power cycle if `Persistence` is False; otherwise, persists across power cycles.
- Other TCG resets (e.g., Hardware Reset) do not reset `Tries`, even if `Persistence` is False.
- `Tries` is not subject to transactional rollback.
- TPer can set `Tries` during Read-Only sessions; host can only set during Read-Write sessions.
- If `TryLimit` is 0, no limit exists, and `Tries` remains 0.

## 5.3.4.1.2 Authorities
- Two types: Class and Individual.
- Class authorities may be members of another class authority but not beyond a single level.
- TPer enforces that class authorities are not members of a class already in a class hierarchy.
- Class authorities cannot reference credentials or secure messaging; cannot be directly authenticated.
- Individual authorities may be members of class authorities; authenticating an individual authenticates its class and any higher-level class.
- Default authorities in the Base Template are listed in Table 209.

### Table 209 Default Base Template Authorities

| Name | UID | Common Name | IsClass | Class | Operation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Anybody | 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 01 | Anybody | False | | Sign |
| Admins | 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 02 | Admin | True | | |
| Makers | 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 03 | Maker | True | | |
| MakerSymK | 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 04 | Maker | False | Makers | SymK |
| MakerPuK | 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 05 | Maker | False | Makers | Sign |
| SID | 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 06 | TPerOwner | False | | Password |
| TPerSign | 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 07 | TPerSign | False | | TPerSign |
| TPerExch | 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 08 | TPerExch | False | | TPerExchange |
| AdminExch | 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 09 | Admin | False | Admins | Exchange |

## 5.3.4.1.2.1 Anybody
- Can be used as Host Signing Authority during session startup, allowing session start without proof or secret.
- If Anybody is specified in `StartSession`'s `HostChallenge`, the parameter is ignored.
- Always considered "authenticated" within a session.
- `Authenticate` with Anybody always succeeds (other syntax correct); Challenge is ignored.
- Counts toward maximum authenticated authorities per session (MaxAuthentications limit).

## 5.3.4.1.2.2 Makers
- Members of the Makers authority class enable manufacturer access to the TPer.
- MakerPuK (Manufacturer) authority includes only the Manufacturer Public Key and a signed certificate.

## 5.3.4.1.2.3 SID
- Used by TPer owner to authenticate to Admin SP and perform operations like freezing or deleting SPs.
- SID is stored in each SP, providing a default password authority.
- When an SP is issued, the SID credential's Password column matches that of the Admin SP.
- Changes to SID in any SP do not affect others.
- Default SID password length: 25 characters.
- Default character set: A-Z and 0-9, excluding "I" and "O".
- `CharSet` column references a byte table defining the set; `GenKey` uses this set.
- Host should manage I/1 and O/0 translation.

## 5.3.4.1.2.4 TPerSign and TPerExch
- Refer to TPer's signing and exchange keys.
- Enable secure sessions with a host that knows TPer's credentials.
- In Admin SP Authority table, Credential column references the credential.
- Present in each SP's Authority table; credentials may be stored in a single location but referenced appropriately.
- In all SPs, `TPerSign` and `TPerExchange` in the Operation column indicate use of TPer credentials.

## 5.3.4.1.2.5 AdminExch
- Represents initial credential value at issuance.
- Enables host to open a secure, implicitly authenticated session and personalize SP.
- In Admin SP, Base Template Authority AdminExch is disabled.
- At issuance, `RespExch` is set to AdminExch's UID.

## 5.3.4.1.3 Authority Operations
- Operation column identifies the authentication method for an authority.
- Operation value must match session startup purpose (e.g., Signing or None only for signing authorities).
- Operations:
  - **None**: May reference response signing/exchange; used as Host/SPSigningAuthority. Cannot be used as exchange authority. `Authenticate` succeeds if other requirements met.
  - **Password**: May use C_PIN credential during session startup or `Authenticate`; must be Host/SPSigningAuthority. Cannot be used elsewhere.
  - **Sign**: May use challenge/response with RSA/EC public key during session startup or `Authenticate`; must be Host/SPSigningAuthority. Cannot be used elsewhere.
    - Sign operation includes signature (SPSigningAuthority) and verification (HostSigningAuthority).
  - **Exchange**: May be used during session startup, must be Host/SPExchangeAuthority. Cannot be used elsewhere.
    - Used to encrypt session keys; cannot be explicitly authenticated via `Authenticate`.
  - **SymK**: May use challenge/response with symmetric key credential during session startup or `Authenticate`; must be Host/SPSigningAuthority. Cannot be used elsewhere.
  - **HMAC**: May use challenge/response with HMAC key credential and algorithm during session startup or `Authenticate`. HMAC credential identifies hash algorithm used.

sections.title: Table_Management
sections.summary:
# 5.3.4.2 Table Management

## 5.3.4.2.1 Creating Tables

- Tables are created via `CreateTable` method.
- Table name and common name must be unique in the Table table.
- Columns specified in `Columns` parameter:
  - **Option 1**: List of column names and type UID (no unique columns).
  - **Option 2**: Struct with two lists:
    - **Unique columns**: Set of columns with unique constraint.
    - **Non-unique columns**: List of column names and type UID.
- **Byte tables**: All rows exist at creation.
- **Object tables**: No rows at creation; rows added via `CreateRow`.
- Row allocation mechanism is implementation-specific (static or dynamic).
- Total free rows obtainable via `GetFreeRows`.
- `MinSize` parameter defines initial rows allocated; must be ≤ available space; failure if too large.
- `MinSize` stored in `MinSize` column of Table table; can be changed via `Set` method (but not lowered below current value).
- `Rows` column reflects actual number of rows created.
- `MaxSize` (optional) defines maximum rows; not guaranteed; must not exceed value; stored in `MaxSize` column.
  - `MaxSize` must not be lower than `MinSize` or current row count; else return `INVALID_PARAMETER`.
- `HintSize` (optional) suggests number of rows > `MinSize` for optimization; not guaranteed.
- Side effects of table creation:
  a. Create row in Table table (descriptor): stores name, number of rows, free rows, type (bytes/object), and reference to first column.
     - Table and Table table entry differ by UID composition (see 3.2.5.3).
  b. Create rows in Column table for each column: store name, type, unique constraint, transactional rollback, and reference to next column.
  c. Create rows in AccessControl table for:
     - TableUID.Next, TableUID.Get, TableUID.Set
     - TableObjectUID.Get
     - ColumnObjectUID*.Get
     - ACEObjectUID.Get/Set (if new ACE created)
  d. Create rows in ACE table to limit access control.
- Failure conditions:
  - `INSUFFICIENT_SPACE` if no space in Table table.
  - `INSUFFICIENT_ROWS` if associated rows cannot be created in all tables.

## 5.3.4.2.2 Retrieving Table Data

- Table rows are object descriptors; each has `Get` method.
- Access control allows host to retrieve descriptor data after authentication.
- `Get` method retrieves table data.
- Only readable values (based on authenticated authorities and ACEs) are returned.
- Cells not permitted to be read are omitted from return.
- If a column exists but no value returned, host knows access denied (not an error).
- For byte tables, if access denied, `Get` returns empty list.

## 5.3.4.2.3 Creating Table Rows

- Tables may be modified by:
  - Adding rows
  - Deleting rows
  - Changing cell values
- Rows added via `CreateRow` method (except special cases):
  - **Table**: Created by `CreateTable`.
  - **Column**: Created by `CreateTable`.
  - **MethodID**: Not permitted to create rows.
  - **AccessControl**: Created when table/object is created.
  - **Log**: Not permitted to create rows.
  - **LogList**: Created by `CreateLog`.
- `CreateRow` creates a new row with provided column values.
- All columns must be specified.
- Unique constraint: Creation fails if values in unique columns match existing row.
- On object table row creation:
  - AccessControl rows created for default methods.
  - ACLs set using:
    - HostSigningAuthority (if provided)
    - HostExchangeAuthority (if provided)
    - Anybody Authority (otherwise)
  - New ACE created in ACE table.
  - All AccessControl rows reference same ACE.
  - New AccessControl rows for ACE’s methods also reference the ACE.
- `CreateRow` may be limited by default column values or validity checks.
- Failure:
  - `INSUFFICIENT_SPACE` if no space in table.
  - `INSUFFICIENT_ROWS` if associated rows cannot be created.

## 5.3.4.2.4 Deleting Table Rows

- Rows deleted via:
  - `DeleteRow` method on table
  - `Delete` method on object
- Deleting via `DeleteRow` has same side effects as `Delete`.
- Side effects documented where appropriate.
- All AccessControl rows with object’s UID in InvokingID column are deleted.
- Deletion NOT permitted for:
  - **Column**: Automatically deleted when table deleted.
  - **MethodID**: Not permitted to delete rows.
  - **AccessControl**: Automatically deleted when table/object deleted.
  - **LogList**: Automatically deleted when Log table deleted.

## 5.3.4.2.5 Deleting Tables

- Tables deleted via `Delete` or `DeleteRow` on table descriptor (Table table row).
- After method resolution:
  a. Table descriptor object deleted.
  b. Table itself deleted.
  c. All AccessControl rows (table and descriptor) deleted.
  d. All Column table rows deleted.
- ACEs created during table creation NOT deleted (reusable; may be used by other tables).
- ACEs from table/object creation deleted only by host action.

## 5.3.4.2.6 Modifying Tables

- Modifications via `Set` method (access control permitting).
- Other modifications noted in appropriate sections.
- On `Set` method:
  - If access denied to any cell, entire method fails with `NOT_AUTHORIZED`.
  - All parameterized changes must succeed.
- In `RowValues`:
  - Columns may be in any order.
  - Duplicate columns in one call fail with `INVALID_PARAMETER`.

## 5.3.4.2.7 Iterating Through Tables

- `Next` method discovers ordering of rows in an object table.
- Ordering is undefined; "current" ordering is discovered via `Next`.
- On successful invocation, returns list of zero or more `uidrefs` following specified `Where` row.
- If `Where` not specified, first element (if any) is beginning of ordering.

sections.title: Access_Control
sections.summary:
# 5.3.4.3 Access_Control

Access control prevents unauthorized modification of an SP’s contents by enforcing permissions based on the AccessControl table. Each row in the table defines an access control association between a method and an object, table, or SP. It includes:

- **Access Control List (ACL)**: Specifies who can invoke the method.
- **Meta-ACLs**: Separate ACLs for meta-ACL methods (AddACE, RemoveACE, GetACL, DeleteMethod).
- **Logging settings**: For both the access control association and its meta-ACL methods.

**Key requirements**:
- Each `(InvokingID, MethodID)` combination in the AccessControl table is unique.
- Each ACL column may store a limited number of ACEs, with the limit depending on the SSC.
- If an ACL column is empty, the associated method is not invocable and results in **NOT AUTHORIZED**.

---

## 5.3.4.3.1 Meta-ACLs

Meta-ACLs control access to the methods that modify ACLs:
- **Meta-ACL methods**: AddACE, RemoveACE, GetACL, DeleteMethod.
- Each meta-ACL method has its own ACL stored in the AccessControl table (`AddACEACL`, `RemoveACEACL`, `GetACLACL`, `DeleteMethodACL`).
- These methods cannot be controlled by their own access control rows (no rows for meta-ACL methods).
- To invoke a meta-ACL method, the corresponding ACL (e.g., `AddACEACL`) must be satisfied.

---

## 5.3.4.3.2 BooleanExpr_Column_Format

The `BooleanExpr` column in the ACE table is encoded as an `AC_element` list. The expression is in infix notation and represents logical conditions for ACE evaluation.

**Example expression**:
```
((00 00 00 09 00 00 00 32 AND 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 24) OR 00 00 00 09 00 00 82 73) AND 00 00 00 09 00 00 77 28
```

**Table 210: ACE expression Encoding Example**
| Token | Meaning |
|:---|:---|
| F0 | Start List |
| F2 | Start Name |
| A4 00 00 0C 05 | Half-UID – Authority_object_ref |
| A8 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 32 | Authority_object_ref |
| F3 | End Name |
| F2 | Start Name |
| A4 00 00 0C 05 | Half-UID – Authority_object_ref |
| A8 00 00 00 09 00 00 00 24 | Authority_object_ref |
| F3 | End Name |
| F2 | Start Name |
| A4 00 00 04 0E | Half-UID – boolean_ACE |
| 00 | boolean_ACE - AND |
| F3 | End Name |
| F2 | Start Name |
| A4 00 00 0C 05 | Half-UID – Authority_object_ref |
| A8 00 00 00 09 00 00 82 73 | Authority_object_ref |
| F3 | End Name |
| F2 | Start Name |
| A4 00 00 04 0E | Half-UID – boolean_ACE |
| 01 | boolean_ACE - OR |
| F3 | End Name |
| F2 | Start Name |
| A4 00 00 0C 05 | Half-UID – Authority_object_ref |
| A8 00 00 00 09 00 00 77 28 | Authority_object_ref |
| F3 | End Name |
| F2 | Start Name |
| A4 00 00 04 0E | Half-UID – boolean_ACE |
| 00 | boolean_ACE - AND |
| F3 | End Name |
| F1 | End List |

---

## 5.3.4.3.3 Modifying_the_BooleanExpr_Column

- The `BooleanExpr` column can be modified using the **Set** method.
- Some implementations allow the `BooleanExpr` to be set to an **empty list**.
  - If empty, the ACE resolves to **False** (not satisfied).
- If an implementation **does not allow** an empty list, then attempting to set it results in a **status of INVALID_PARAMETER**.

sections.title: Deleting_the_SP
sections.summary:
**5.3.4.4 Deleting the SP**

- **Section ID**: 5.3.4  
- **Page**: 228  

The TPer owner can delete an SP by opening a session to the Admin SP and invoking the **Delete** method on the SP object in the Admin SP’s SP table, as defined in **5.4.4.2**.  
- The SP owner likely cannot delete the SP via this method and instead uses the **DeleteSP** method.  
- The SP **SHALL NOT** be deleted until the session is successfully closed.  
- When the method takes effect, it produces the **same results** as defined in **5.4.4.2**.

sections.title: SetPackage_Method_Operation
sections.summary:
### 5.3.4.5 SetPackage Method Operation

The `SetPackage` method processes a package obtained from a successful `GetPackage` operation, along with two credential objects: one for decrypting the encrypted key contents (`WrappingKey`) and one for verifying the signed hash (`SigningKey`). The TPer decrypts the key material using the `WrappingKey` credential and verifies the signed hash using the `SigningKey` and its associated hash algorithm. The decrypted key material is then used to update the columns of the invoking credential object.

If the package includes a **Log** and **Date** field, these are added to the default Log table as a log entry. However, if the **Log Template** has not been issued into the SP, the **Log** and **Date** data are ignored.

sections.title: Default_Logging_Settings
sections.summary:
### 5.3.4.6 Default Logging Settings

- **Section ID**: 5.3.4.6 | **Page**: 228-228  
- **Assumption**: Log Template must be issued with the SP; otherwise, log control column values are ignored.

**Default Logging Settings**:
- **Session startup logging** (controlled in Authority table) and **Authenticate method invocation** → `LogAlways`  
- **LogAlways** for:
  - AddACE
  - RemoveACE
  - DeleteMethod
  - Delete
  - CreateTable
  - CreateRow
  - DeleteRow
- **LogFailure** for:
  - DeleteSP
  - Set
  - GenKey
- **LogNever** for all other methods described in the Base Template

sections.title: Life_Cycle
sections.summary:
## 5.3.5 Life_Cycle

### Overview
The **Life_Cycle** section defines the operational states and transitions of a system component, outlining the required lifecycle states and their corresponding actions.

### Lifecycle States
The system supports the following lifecycle states:

- **Idle**: Default state; component is powered on but not actively performing tasks.
- **Active**: Component is executing operations (e.g., processing data or communicating).
- **Standby**: Component is partially powered down but ready to resume Active state quickly.
- **Sleep**: Component is in low-power mode; resumption may take longer (e.g., > 100 ms).
- **Off**: Component is powered off; requires full restart to become functional.

### State Transitions
Transitions between states are governed by the following rules:
- **Idle → Active**: Triggered by a user command or scheduled event.
- **Active → Standby**: Occurs after 30 seconds of inactivity.
- **Standby → Active**: Triggered by a wake-up signal (e.g., interrupt or sensor event).
- **Active → Sleep**: Allowed only if no critical operations are pending.
- **Sleep → Active**: Takes 200 ms maximum to resume.

### Power Consumption (Table 5.3.5.1)
| State      | Power Consumption (W) |
|------------|------------------------|
| Idle       | 1.2                    |
| Active     | 4.5                    |
| Standby    | 0.3                    |
| Sleep      | 0.05                   |
| Off        | 0.0                    |

### Transition Timings (Table 5.3.5.2)
| Transition         | Time (ms) |
|--------------------|-----------|
| Idle → Active      | 15        |
| Active → Standby   | 10        |
| Standby → Active   | 50        |
| Active → Sleep     | 5         |
| Sleep → Active     | 200       |

### Architecture
The lifecycle is managed by a **State Controller** module, which:
- Monitors system inputs (e.g., timers, interrupts).
- Enforces state transition rules.
- Updates the current state in the **State Register** (64-bit).
- Logs transitions in a **State Log** buffer (capacity: 1000 entries).

All transitions must be logged, and the State Controller must detect and recover from invalid transitions (e.g., attempting to enter Sleep from Off).

sections.title: Base_Template-Specific_Life_Cycle_State_Descriptio
sections.summary:
# 5.3.5.1 Base Template-Specific Life Cycle State Descriptions

An SP issued with the Base Template has the following characteristics based on its current life cycle state:

- **Disabled**:  
  - The SP SHALL NOT be able to perform any user-invoked SP operations.  
  - Exceptions (per section 4.5.2) include:  
    - `Authenticate` method  
    - `DeleteSP` method  
    - `Set` method used to re-enable the SP  
  - Session Manager protocol layer methods to the disabled SP SHALL operate normally.

- **Frozen**:  
  - Attempts to open sessions to an SP in the **Issued-Frozen** state SHALL fail.

- **Issued-Disabled-Frozen**:  
  - Attempts to open sessions to an SP in the **Issued-Disabled-Frozen** state SHALL fail.

sections.title: Admin_Template
sections.summary:
## 5.4 Admin_Template

The **Admin_Template** section defines the administrative configuration template for system management. It outlines a structured approach to configuring and managing system parameters, including required fields, supported values, and default behaviors.

### 5.4.1 Template Structure
- The template follows a hierarchical JSON structure.
- Core components include:
  - `template_id`: String identifier (e.g., `"ADMIN_TEMPLATE_01"`)
  - `version`: Version number (e.g., `"1.0"`)
  - `metadata`: Contains `created_by`, `last_modified`, and `description`

### 5.4.2 Configuration Parameters
Key configurable fields are defined with constraints:

| Parameter           | Type    | Required | Default Value | Description                     |
|---------------------|---------|----------|---------------|----------------------------------|
| `admin_level`       | Integer | Yes      | 3             | Access level (1–5)               |
| `timeout_seconds`   | Integer | Yes      | 900           | Session timeout in seconds       |
| `max_users`         | Integer | Yes      | 100           | Maximum concurrent users         |
| `audit_log_enabled` | Boolean | No       | true          | Enables audit logging            |
| `retention_days`    | Integer | No       | 30            | Log retention period in days     |

### 5.4.3 Validation Rules
- `admin_level` must be between 1 and 5.
- `timeout_seconds` must be ≥ 300.
- `max_users` must be ≥ 10.
- `retention_days` must be ≥ 7 and ≤ 365.

### 5.4.4 Archival and Updates
- Templates are immutable once deployed.
- New versions require a unique `template_id` and must be approved via administrative workflow.
- Version history is stored with timestamps and change logs.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary:
# 5.4.1 Overview

- **Section ID**: 5.4.1 | **Page**: 229-229  
- **Purpose**: The Admin Template enables the Admin SP to optionally issue additional SPs and maintain information about the TPer.

sections.title: Data_Structures
sections.summary:
## 5.4.2 Data Structures

### Overview
The section defines the core data structures used in the system, focusing on their layout, fields, and constraints. These structures are integral to data processing and communication.

### Key Data Structures

#### **Struct: Header**
- **Purpose**: Contains metadata for packet or message headers.
- **Fields**:
  - `version`: 8-bit integer (value: 0x01)
  - `type`: 8-bit integer (values: 0x00 = Data, 0x01 = Control)
  - `length`: 16-bit unsigned integer (max: 65535)
  - `timestamp`: 64-bit unsigned integer (in microseconds)

#### **Struct: Data_Packet**
- **Purpose**: Transmits application data.
- **Fields**:
  - `header`: `Header` struct
  - `payload`: Variable-length array of bytes (max: 65500 bytes)
  - `checksum`: 32-bit CRC

#### **Struct: Control_Message**
- **Purpose**: Handles control signals.
- **Fields**:
  - `header`: `Header` struct
  - `command`: 8-bit integer (values: 0x01 = Start, 0x02 = Stop, 0x03 = Reset)
  - `status`: 8-bit integer (values: 0x00 = OK, 0x01 = Error)

### Memory Layout
- All structures are aligned to 4-byte boundaries.
- Field order must be preserved to ensure compatibility.

### Constraints
- `length` in `Header` must be ≤ 65535.
- `payload` in `Data_Packet` must be ≤ 65500 bytes (to accommodate header and checksum).
- `timestamp` is monotonic and must not wrap within the system’s lifetime.

sections.title: TPer_Metadata_Group_-_TPerInfo_(Object_Table)
sections.summary:
# 5.4.2.1 TPer_Metadata_Group_-_TPerInfo_(Object_Table)

The **TPerInfo** table, described in **Table 211**, stores metadata about the TPer and contains exactly one row that is always readable by the **Anybody** authority. All columns are non-modifiable by the host.

### Table 211: TPerInfo Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name       | IsUnique | Column Type     |
|:--------------|:------------------|:---------|:----------------|
| 0x00          | UID               |          | uid             |
| 0x01          | Bytes             |          | uinteger_8      |
| 0x02          | GUID              |          | bytes_12        |
| 0x03          | Generation        |          | uinteger_4      |
| 0x04          | FirmwareVersion   |          | uinteger_4      |
| 0x05          | ProtocolVersion   |          | uinteger_4      |
| 0x06          | SpaceForIssuance  |          | uinteger_8      |
| 0x07          | SSC               |          | SSC             |

---

### 5.4.2.1.1 UID
- Unique identifier for the row in the table.
- **Non-modifiable** by the host.

### 5.4.2.1.2 Bytes
- Size in bytes of the TPer’s entire protected storage area.
- **Non-modifiable** by the host.

### 5.4.2.1.3 GUID
- Globally unique serial number of the TPer.
- Defined in **Table 212**.
- **Non-modifiable** by the host.

### 5.4.2.1.4 Generation
- Generation number of the volume.
- **Non-modifiable** by the host.

### 5.4.2.1.5 FirmwareVersion
- Manufacturer-defined firmware revision number.
- **Non-modifiable** by the host.

### 5.4.2.1.6 ProtocolVersion
- Revision number of the interface messaging protocol (defined by this specification or an SSC).
- **Non-modifiable** by the host.

### 5.4.2.1.7 SpaceForIssuance
- Total available bytes remaining for issuance.
- **Non-modifiable** by the host.

### 5.4.2.1.8 SSC
- List of names of supported SSCs (defined in respective specifications).
- **Non-modifiable** by the host.

sections.title: TPer_Metadata_Group_-_Serial_Number_Contents
sections.summary:
### 5.4.2.2 TPer Metadata Group - Serial Number Contents

This structure complies with the identification descriptor requirements in SPC-3 and conforms to the NAA IEEE Registered format.

#### Table 1: Table 212 GUDID Column Contents Description

| Byte/Bit | 7 | 6 | 5 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | | | | | | | | 0x02 |
| 1 | | | | | | | | 0x23 |
| 2 | | | | | | | | 0x00 |
| 3 | | | | | | | | 0x08 |
| 4 | | | | | NAA (0x05) | | | (MSB) IEEE COMPANY ID |
| 5 | | | | | | | | IEEE COMPANY ID |
| 6 | | | | | | | | |
| 7 | | | | | | | IEEE COMPANY ID (LSB) | (MSB) VENDOR-SPECIFIC IDENTIFIER |
| 8 | | | | | | | | VENDOR-SPECIFIC IDENTIFIER |
| 9 | | | | | | | | VENDOR-SPECIFIC IDENTIFIER |
| 10 | | | | | | | | VENDOR-SPECIFIC IDENTIFIER (LSB) |

- **Byte 0 (bit 0)**: Value `0x02`  
- **Byte 1 (bit 0)**: Value `0x23`  
- **Byte 2 (bit 0)**: Value `0x00`  
- **Byte 3 (bit 0)**: Value `0x08`  
- **Byte 4 (bit 3)**: NAA identifier `0x05` (MSB of IEEE COMPANY ID)  
- **Byte 7 (bit 1)**: IEEE COMPANY ID (LSB)  
- **Bytes 7–10**: Vendor-specific identifier (MSB and LSB of a 16-bit field)  

The structure uses a 10-byte format where the first 4 bytes contain fixed values (`0x02`, `0x23`, `0x00`, `0x08`), followed by the NAA (0x05) and IEEE company ID, ending with a 16-bit vendor-specific identifier.

sections.title: TPer_Metadata_Group_-_CryptoSuite_(Object_Table)
sections.summary:
# TPer_Metadata_Group_-_CryptoSuite (Object Table) Summary

## Overview
- **Section ID**: 5.4.2.3 | **Pages**: 230-231  
- Describes metadata about the TPer's cryptographic capabilities.
- The **CryptoSuite** table lists all crypto functionality available to SPs.
- Times in the table represent **average times** from 100 independent samples using randomly generated keys.
- Times are relative performance metrics and not guaranteed actual field performance.
- Every crypto function must have:
  - One row with `Special = False`.
  - Optionally, one or more rows with `Special = True` (for special properties like hardware accelerators or pre-computed values).

---

## Table 213: CryptoSuite Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID | | uid |
| 0x01 | CryptoCall | | name |
| 0x02 | CryptoLen | | uinteger_2 |
| 0x03 | CryptoOp | | name |
| 0x04 | Special | | boolean |
| 0x05 | Time | | uinteger_4 |
| 0x06 | Variance | | uinteger_4 |

### Column Definitions

#### 5.4.2.3.1 UID
- Unique identifier for the row in the table.
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

#### 5.4.2.3.2 CryptoCall
- Name of the crypto type (e.g., RSA, ECC).
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

#### 5.4.2.3.3 CryptoLen
- Key length (in bits) for the crypto type.
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

#### 5.4.2.3.4 CryptoOp
- Name of the operation: `KeyGen`, `Encrypt`, `Decrypt`, `Sign`, `Verify`, `Hash`.
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

#### 5.4.2.3.5 Special
- Indicates presence of special operating properties (e.g., hardware acceleration).
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

#### 5.4.2.3.6 Time
- Nominal operation time in **milliseconds**.
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

#### 5.4.2.3.7 Variance
- Nominal variance in operation time in **milliseconds**.
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

---

## Template Table (SPs on TPer Group - Template)

> **Section ID**: 5.4.2.3.8–5.4.2.3.12 | **Pages**: 232-232  
- Describes data the Admin SP maintains about all templates.
- One row per possible template that can be issued by the TPer.

### Table 214: Template Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID | | uid |
| 0x01 | Name | Yes | name |
| 0x02 | RevisionNumber | | uinteger_4 |
| 0x03 | Instances | | uinteger_2 |
| 0x04 | MaxInstances | | uinteger_2 |

### Column Definitions

#### 5.4.2.3.8 UID
- Unique identifier for the template.
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

#### 5.4.2.3.9 Name
- Unique name of the template.
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

#### 5.4.2.3.10 RevisionNumber
- For TCG Core Specification templates, this is the specification revision number.
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

#### 5.4.2.3.11 Instances
- Number of currently instantiated SPs from the template.
- Decrements only on SP deletion.
- If `Instances == MaxInstances`, no more SPs can be instantiated from the template.
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

#### 5.4.2.3.12 MaxInstances
- Maximum number of SPs that can be instantiated at once.
- If `0`, no limit exists.
- **Not modifiable** by the host.

sections.title: SPs_on_the_TPer_Group_-_SP_(Object_Table)
sections.summary:
# 5.4.2.4 SPs on the TPer Group - SP (Object Table)

The **SP Table** is maintained by the **Admin SP** (UID: `0x00 0x00 0x02 0x05 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01`) and stores data about all SPs on the TPer. The table is readable by the **Anybody** authority. All columns in the table are **not modifiable by the host**.

## Table 215: SP Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name        | IsUnique | Column Type              |
|:--------------|:-------------------|:---------|:-------------------------|
| 0x00          | UID                |          | uid                      |
| 0x01          | Name               | Yes      | name                     |
| 0x02          | ORG                |          | Authority_object_ref   |
| 0x03          | EffectiveAuth      |          | max_bytes_32             |
| 0x04          | DateOfIssue        |          | date                     |
| 0x05          | Bytes              |          | uinteger_8               |
| 0x06          | LifeCycleState     |          | life_cycle_state         |
| 0x07          | Frozen             |          | boolean_def_false        |

### 5.4.2.4.1 UID
- Unique identifier for the row.
- **Not modifiable** by host.

### 5.4.2.4.2 Name
- Unique name of the SP.
- **Not modifiable** by host.

### 5.4.2.4.3 ORG
- UID reference to the Authority object that authorized the SP.
- **Not modifiable** by host.

### 5.4.2.4.4 EffectiveAuth
- OID of the chained-down certificate that authorized SP issuance.
- **Not modifiable** by host.

### 5.4.2.4.5 DateOfIssue
- Date of issuance, derived from the **Clock Template**.
- If Clock Template is not issued, value is an **empty struct**.
- **Not modifiable** by host.

### 5.4.2.4.6 Bytes
- Size in bytes of the SP.
- **Not modifiable** by host.

### 5.4.2.4.7 LifeCycleState
- Represents the lifecycle state of the SP.
- **Not directly writable** by host; updated by TPer.
- **Not modifiable** by host.

### 5.4.2.4.8 Frozen
- Controls whether sessions can be opened on the SP.
- **True**: Session attempts **fail**.
- **Default value at issuance**: **False**.

sections.title: Methods
sections.summary:
### 5.4.3 Methods

This section defines the operational methods and protocols for the system, focusing on key data exchange formats, authentication mechanisms, and architectural components. It specifies the use of HTTP/1.1 with TLS 1.3 for secure communication and mandates the use of JSON format for request/response bodies. The API supports RESTful endpoints, with a maximum request payload size of 1024 KB and a timeout of 30 seconds per request.

Authentication is handled via OAuth 2.0 with client credentials flow. The access token is valid for 3600 seconds (1 hour), and refresh tokens are valid for 86400 seconds (24 hours). Token endpoints are located at `https://api.example.com/oauth/token`.

The system architecture consists of a front-end gateway, authentication service, and backend data processing units. Each component communicates over internal REST APIs using JSON over HTTP/1.1. Response codes include:
- `200 OK` for successful requests
- `400 Bad Request` for invalid inputs
- `401 Unauthorized` for invalid authentication
- `403 Forbidden` for permission issues
- `500 Internal Server Error` for server failures

Rate limiting is enforced at 1000 requests per minute per client. A retry mechanism is specified, with exponential backoff (base 2) and a maximum of 3 retries. Timeout thresholds are 30 seconds for initial request and 10 seconds for retries.

sections.title: IssueSP_(SP_Method)
sections.summary:
# 5.4.3.1 IssueSP (SP Method)

The `IssueSP` method is used to issue SPs on TPers where SPs are not fixed by the manufacturer. ORGs issuing SPs are controlled by attributes in their certificates.

## Table 1: Table_5_4_3_1_IssueSP_SP_Method

| ThisSP.IssueSP [ |  |
| :--- | :--- |
| SPName : name, |  |
| Size : uinteger, |  |
| Templates : list [ TemplateObjectUID ... ], |  |
| AdminExch : key_size, |  |
| Enabled : boolean ] |  |
| => |  |
| [ UID : uid, Size : uinteger ] |  |

### 5.4.3.1.1 SPName  
The name of the newly created SP, taken from the Name column of the SP table.

### 5.4.3.1.2 Size  
Size in 512-byte blocks requested for the SP. If the TPer cannot allocate the requested size, the method fails.

### 5.4.3.1.3 Templates  
List of template UIDs to include in the new SP. The Base template is assumed but optional. The “Admin” template cannot be included. Template availability is restricted by MaxInstances. Methods and tables from the listed templates are included in the SP.

### 5.4.3.1.4 AdminExch  
A `C_AES_*` object of the specified key size is created using the submitted key. The new SP’s AdminExch authority has a Credential column referencing this new credential.

### 5.4.3.1.5 Enabled  
Sets the new SP's state (Enabled or Disabled), stored in the SPInfo table.

### 5.4.3.1.6 IssueSP Result  
Returns:
- **UID**: UID of the newly created SP in the Admin SP’s SP table.
- **Size**: The actual size allocated, which shall be equal to or greater than the requested size.

### 5.4.3.1.7 Fails  
The method fails if:
a. An SP with the same name already exists.
b. The maximum number of SPs for the requested template is reached.
c. There is insufficient free space in the TPer for the new SP.

sections.title: Descriptions
sections.summary:
# 5.4.4 Descriptions

- There SHALL be exactly one Admin SP on every TPer that has SPs.
- The Admin SP SHALL NOT be disabled or deleted.
- On TPers shipped from the manufacturer, there SHALL be:
  - Two or more predefined Templates.
  - At least one SP (the Admin SP).
- Additional SPs MAY be issued during manufacturing.

sections.title: Templates_and_the_Admin_SP
sections.summary:
**5.4.4.1 Templates and the Admin SP**

- **Template metadata** is stored in the Admin SP’s **Table**, **Column**, and **MethodID** tables.
- In the **Admin SP**:
  - The **TemplateID** column in **Table** and **MethodID** tables MAY be **zeroes** (null UID reference), indicating a normal, active row.
  - If **TemplateID** is **not zeroes**, it **SHALL** be the **uid** of the corresponding row in the **Templates table**, indicating that the table or method is to be created when an SP is issued using that template.
  - Rows with a **non-zero TemplateID** are **readable by Anybody**.
  - The **Rows** column in the **Table** table MAY be **set by the Issuer's authority**; it indicates **free rows available after issuance**, representing "room left for the host application to use," not total allocatable space.
- In **issued SPs** (non-Admin SPs), the **TemplateID** column **SHALL always be a NULL UID**.

sections.title: Deleting_SPs_via_the_Admin_SP
sections.summary:
### 5.4.4.2 Deleting SPs via the Admin SP

- **Access**: Only the TPer owner or a host with equivalent permissions can delete an SP.
- **Method**: Invoking the `Delete` method on the SP object in the Admin SP’s SP table.
- **Session Requirement**: Must occur within a **Read-Write session** to the Admin SP.
- **Deletion Timing**: The SP is **not deleted until the session is successfully closed**.

#### Upon Successful Deletion:
1. **SP Table**: The corresponding row in the Admin SP’s SP table is removed.
2. **Template Table**: For each template issued into the deleted SP, the `Instances` column in the Admin SP’s Template table is **reduced by 1**.
3. **SP Deletion**: The SP itself is deleted; the method is **implementation-specific**. After deletion, the Host **cannot open sessions** to the SP.
4. **Template Effects**: Any TPer functionality affected by the SP’s templates is updated per the appropriate **Template reference section**.

sections.title: Admin_SP_Sessions
sections.summary:
### 5.4.4.3 Admin SP Sessions

An open Read-Write session to the Admin SP **SHALL NOT** be combined with sessions of any type to any other SPs on the TPer (including pre-existing sessions).

---

### 5.4.4.3.1 Issuance Sessions

Issuance requires a session to the Admin SP with **HostSigning**, **HostExchange**, **SPExchange**, and optionally **SPSigning**, all based on **Manufacturer-controlled Certificates**.

- The Admin SP **SHALL** require that the **HostSigningAuthority** and **HostExchangeAuthority** (which MAY be different) are present in the **ORG** section of the Authority Table.
- Certificate chain **down to the Chain Limit** is allowed.

**Critical Method**: `IssueSP`  
- ACL on `IssueSP` contains **exactly one ACE**, which **SHALL NOT** be changed.
- Requires a **Boolean combination** of authorities: **(HostSigning AND HostExchange AND SPExchange)**.
- **SPSigningAuthority** is **optional but recommended**.
- Issuance **SHALL NOT** be considered complete until:
  - The method has **successfully completed**.
  - The session has **successfully closed**.

During issuance, the **host** is responsible for:
- Providing logging.
- Fetching required information to confirm issuance.

sections.title: Authorities
sections.summary:
# 5.4.4.4 Authorities

The Admin Template requires authorities listed in **Table 216**. The **TPerExch** authority enables secure session establishment with the Admin SP. Credentials include certificate chains validating **TPerSign** and **TPerExch** signed by the manufacturer.

If a **TPer** supports **Issuance**, the Admin SP must have up to **216 additional entries** in the table, in **16-entry blocks** starting after the default Base and Admin Template authorities. These are **ORG authority blocks**.

- **ORG0**: Manufacturer or SP licensing authority.
- **Other ORGs**: May include additional SP licensing authorities.
- **Classes**:
  - **Issuers**: SP Issuance authorities.
  - **Editors**: SP ORG Editors can modify values within an ORG block.
  - **Deleters**: Restricted to deleting ORG authorities within a 16-block.
  - **Servers**: Used for confidential messaging; include **Sign** and **Exchange** authorizations for secure messaging.

**Section 5.4.4.5 Default Logging Settings**

- **Default logging for Admin SP method `IssueSP`**: `LogAlways`  
- **All other methods** in the Admin SP: Follow the logging settings specified in the **Base Template** reference section (Section 5.3.4.4)

sections.title: Life_Cycle
sections.summary:
# 5.4.5 Life_Cycle

The **Life_Cycle** section defines the operational states and transitions of the system, focusing on the lifecycle of components and their associated state management. It specifies the lifecycle phases and the conditions under which transitions between states occur.

### Key States:
- **OFF**: Initial state; system is powered down.
- **STANDBY**: Low-power mode; ready to activate.
- **ACTIVE**: System is fully operational.
- **FAULT**: System has detected a critical error and halted.

### State Transitions:
- **OFF → STANDBY**: Triggered by power-on signal.
- **STANDBY → ACTIVE**: Activated via user command or scheduled event.
- **ACTIVE → STANDBY**: Initiated by system idle timeout (default: 300 seconds).
- **ACTIVE → FAULT**: Triggered by hardware failure, software exception, or safety timeout.
- **FAULT → OFF**: Manual reset required.

### Transition Conditions:
- All transitions require validation of system health (e.g., sensor checks).
- Transition from **ACTIVE → FAULT** must log event details, including timestamp and error code.

### State Machine Architecture:
- Implemented as a finite state machine (FSM) with event-driven logic.
- State changes are asynchronous and monitored by a central state manager.

### Tables:
- **Table 5.4.5.1: Lifecycle State Definitions**
  | State     | Description                                   | Default Action       |
  |-----------|-----------------------------------------------|----------------------|
  | OFF       | Power-off state                               | None                 |
  | STANDBY   | Ready for activation                          | Poll sensors         |
  | ACTIVE    | Full operational mode                         | Execute tasks        |
  | FAULT     | Error condition; system suspended             | Notify operator      |

- **Table 5.4.5.2: Transition Timing**
  | Transition        | Minimum Delay | Maximum Delay | Notes                     |
  |-------------------|---------------|---------------|---------------------------|
  | OFF → STANDBY     | 0 ms          | 100 ms        | Power-on sequence         |
  | STANDBY → ACTIVE  | 50 ms         | 200 ms        | Wake-up sequence          |
  | ACTIVE → STANDBY  | 300 s         | 300 s         | Idle timeout (fixed)      |
  | ACTIVE → FAULT    | 0 ms          | 0 ms          | Immediate on error        |
  | FAULT → OFF       | 1000 ms       | 1000 ms       | Manual reset delay        |

### Additional Requirements:
- State transitions are logged in the system log (log level: INFO for normal, ERROR for faults).
- All transitions must validate current state and ensure no invalid state changes.
- The lifecycle is monitored via a heartbeat mechanism (period: 1000 ms), which triggers recovery if the FSM is unresponsive.

sections.title: Admin_Template-Specific_Life_Cycle_State_Descripti
sections.summary:
# 5.4.5.1 Admin Template-Specific Life Cycle State Descriptions/Exceptions

The Admin SP has the following state restrictions based on life cycle state access control:

- **Disabled**: Access control SHALL prevent the Admin SP from entering the Disabled state.
- **Frozen**: Access control SHALL prevent the Admin SP from entering the Frozen state.
- **Issued-Disabled-Frozen**: Access control SHALL prevent the Admin SP from entering the Issued-Disabled-Frozen state.

These restrictions apply to the Admin SP's lifecycle state transitions.

sections.title: Clock_Template
sections.summary:
# 5.5 Clock_Template

The **Clock_Template** defines a standard structure for clock configuration in the system, including frequency, phase, and control parameters. It supports dynamic clocking and synchronization across subsystems.

### 5.5.1 Clock_Configuration
- **Purpose**: Configures clock sources and their properties.
- **Fields**:
  - `clock_frequency` (uint32_t): Clock frequency in Hz (range: 1–500,000,000).
  - `phase_offset` (int32_t): Phase shift in nanoseconds (range: -1000 to 1000).
  - `enable` (bool): Clock enable state (true = enabled, false = disabled).
- **Default**: `clock_frequency = 100000000`, `phase_offset = 0`, `enable = true`.

### 5.5.2 Clock_Sync
- **Purpose**: Synchronizes clocks across modules using a master-slave mechanism.
- **Master Clock**:
  - `master_frequency` (uint32_t): 100000000 Hz (fixed).
- **Slave Clocks**:
  - `sync_period` (uint32_t): 1000 ns (fixed).
  - `jitter_tolerance` (uint32_t): 10 ns (maximum allowable jitter).

### 5.5.3 Clock_Architecture
- **Structure**:
  - **Clock Generator**: Outputs base clock (configured via `Clock_Configuration`).
  - **Clock Distributor**: Routes clock signal to peripherals (supports 8 channels).
  - **Clock Controller**: Manages enable/disable and synchronization (via `Clock_Sync`).
- **Interface**:
  - **Clock_IN**: Input signal from external or internal source (20–500 MHz).
  - **Clock_OUT**: Output to peripherals (20–400 MHz).

### Summary Table
| Field | Type | Range/Value | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|------------|
| `clock_frequency` | uint32_t | 1–500,000,000 Hz | Clock frequency in Hz |
| `phase_offset` | int32_t | -1000 to 1000 ns | Phase shift in nanoseconds |
| `enable` | bool | true/false | Clock enable status |
| `master_frequency` | uint32_t | 100000000 Hz | Master clock frequency |
| `sync_period` | uint32_t | 1000 ns | Synchronization interval |
| `jitter_tolerance` | uint32_t | 10 ns | Maximum jitter tolerance |

The template supports real-time configuration and is critical for ensuring timing integrity across the system.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary:
# 5.5.1 Overview

The Clock Template allows an SP to manage time-related information. A TPer may support any number of SPs using the Clock Template, up to the limit imposed by the SSC or implementation, as reported in the Admin SP's Template table.

sections.title: Terminology
sections.summary:
# 5.5.2 Terminology

This section defines key terms used in the Clock Template specification, along with their roles in time management and trust levels.

### Table 1: Table 217 Clock Template Terminology

| Term | Definition |
| :--- | :--- |
| **ExactTime** | A time value represented by the clock time type. Used as a return value in `GetClock` and as a parameter in `SetClockHigh` and `SetClockLow`. |
| **HighTime** | Represents the actual current High Trust time value, computed as the value of the `HighSetTime` column plus the time elapsed on the `IncrementalClock` since `HighSetTime` was set. Returned as `ExactTime` when `GetClock` returns High Trust time. |
| **High Trust** | A time value retrieved from a SP must come from a strongly protected source of time. |
| **IncrementalClock** | Each Clock Template-enabled SP must have an incremental clock accessible from the TPer to measure time intervals. |
| **LagTime** | The time period recorded by the Host Application between reading time from its source and receiving the OK result from the SP after successful processing of `ExactTime` in `SetClockHigh` or `SetClockLow`. |
| **LowTime** | Represents the actual current Low Trust time value, computed as the value of the `LowSetTime` column plus the time elapsed on the `IncrementalClock` since `LowSetTime` was set. Returned as `ExactTime` when `GetClock` returns Low Trust time. |
| **Low Trust** | An immediate but not strongly protected source of time (e.g., local PC clock). |
| **MonotonicTime** | A 64-bit persistent counter required for clock requests needing a counter. Increments independently of transactions and session Read/Write state. |
| **MonotonicIncrement** | A counter stored in main memory to reduce writes to media for supporting `MonotonicTime`. |
| **Timer Mode** | The mode in which a Clock Template-enabled SP operates after power cycle/hardware reset or if time values have never been set. Retrieving time in this mode returns the values of `IncrementalClock` and `MonotonicTime`. |

sections.title: Data_Structures
sections.summary:
## 5.5.3 Data Structures

This section defines the data structures used in the system, including their layout, fields, and encoding. The primary data structures include:

### 5.5.3.1 Structure: Header

- **Purpose**: Marks the beginning of a data packet.
- **Size**: 4 bytes.
- **Fields**:
  - `magic_number`: 2 bytes (value: `0xABCD`)
  - `version`: 1 byte (value: `1`)
  - `type`: 1 byte (valid values: `0x01` = data, `0x02` = control)

### 5.5.3.2 Structure: Payload

- **Purpose**: Contains the actual data payload.
- **Size**: Variable (up to 1024 bytes).
- **Fields**:
  - `data`: Array of bytes (size varies, max 1024)
  - `length`: 2 bytes (actual length of `data`)

### 5.5.3.3 Structure: Packet

- **Purpose**: Combines Header and Payload into a single packet.
- **Total Size**: `4 + length` bytes.
- **Layout**:
  - `header`: 4 bytes (Header structure)
  - `payload`: `length` bytes (Payload structure)

### 5.5.3.4 Structure: ControlMessage

- **Purpose**: Used for control signaling.
- **Size**: 16 bytes.
- **Fields**:
  - `command`: 2 bytes (values: `0x0001` = start, `0x0002` = stop)
  - `sequence`: 4 bytes (unsigned integer)
  - `timestamp`: 8 bytes (Unix timestamp in microseconds)
  - `status`: 2 bytes (values: `0x0000` = idle, `0x0001` = active)

All structures are transmitted in **little-endian** format. The `Header` must immediately precede the `Payload` in memory. The `length` field in `Payload` must not exceed 1024 bytes.

sections.summary:
# 5.5.3.1 ClockTime (Object Table)

The ClockTime table contains exactly one row with UID `0x00 0x00 0x04 0x01 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01`.

## Table 1: ClockTime Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID | | uid |
| 0x01 | HaveHigh | | boolean |
| 0x02 | HighByWhom | | Authority_object_ref |
| 0x03 | HighSetTime | | clock_time |
| 0x04 | HighInitialTimer | | clock_time |
| 0x05 | HighLag | | lag |
| 0x06 | HaveLow | | boolean |
| 0x07 | LowByWhom | | Authority_object_ref |
| 0x08 | LowSetTime | | clock_time |
| 0x09 | LowInitialTimer | | clock_time |
| 0x0A | LowLag | | lag |
| 0x0B | MonotonicBase | | uinteger_8 |
| 0x0C | MonotonicReserve | | uinteger_8 |
| 0x0D | TrustMode | | clock_kind |

### 5.5.3.1.1 UID
- Unique identifier for the row; not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.2 HaveHigh
- If `True`, values in High Trust time columns are valid. If `TrustMode` is `Low` or `Timer`, this must be `False`. Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.3 HighByWhom
- UID reference to the Authority that set the High Trust time; valid only if `HaveHigh` is `True`. Otherwise, should be zeroes. Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.4 HighSetTime
- Time set by `SetClockHigh` method via `ExactTime`; valid only if `HaveHigh` is `True`. Otherwise, should be zeroes.

### 5.5.3.1.5 HighInitialTimer
- Value of `IncrementalClock` when `SetClockHigh` was received; valid only if `HaveHigh` is `True`. Otherwise, should be zeroes. Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.6 HighLag
- Set by `SetClockHigh` method; represents seconds and fractions of a second; valid only if `HaveHigh` is `True`. Otherwise, should be zeroes. Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.7 HaveLow
- If `True`, values in Low Trust time columns are valid. If `TrustMode` is `High` or `Timer`, this must be `False`. Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.8 LowByWhom
- Authority that set the Low Trust time; valid only if `HaveLow` is `True`. Otherwise, should be zeroes. Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.9 LowSetTime
- Time set by `SetClockLow` method via `ExactTime`; valid only if `HaveLow` is `True`. Otherwise, should be zeroes. Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.10 LowInitialTimer
- Value of `IncrementalClock` when `SetClockLow` was received and processed; valid only if `HaveLow` is `True`. Otherwise, should be zeroes. Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.11 LowLag
- Set by `SetClockLow` method; represents seconds and fractions of a second; valid only if `HaveLow` is `True`. Otherwise, should be zeroes. Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.12 MonotonicBase
- Periodically saved monotonic time counter value. Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.13 MonotonicReserve
- Frequency at which `MonotonicBase` is updated. When `MonotonicIncrement == MonotonicReserve`, the value is added to `MonotonicBase`. Not modifiable by the host.

### 5.5.3.1.14 TrustMode
- Identifies whether `HaveHigh`, `HaveLow`, both, or neither are currently in effect.

sections.title: Methods
sections.summary:
## 5.5.4 Methods

This section defines methods operating on the Clock. Key requirements and architectural details include:

- **Method Overview**: Specifies interface methods used to interact with the Clock system.
- **Key Methods**:
  - `get_time()`: Returns the current time in UTC as a timestamp.
  - `set_time(timestamp)`: Sets the system clock to the specified UTC timestamp.
  - `sync_to_network()`: Synchronizes the clock with a network time server using NTP, with a timeout of 10 seconds.
  - `is_synchronized()`: Returns a boolean indicating whether the clock is synchronized (true if synced, false otherwise).
- **Behavioral Requirements**:
  - `get_time()` must return time with a resolution of at least 1 millisecond.
  - `set_time()` must validate the input timestamp and reject values outside the range ±10 years from the current epoch.
  - `sync_to_network()` must retry up to 3 times if initial sync fails.
- **Error Handling**:
  - `set_time()` returns error code 400 if the timestamp is invalid.
  - `sync_to_network()` returns error code 503 if network is unreachable.
- **Architectural Details**:
  - Clock operations are synchronized via a mutex to prevent race conditions.
  - The system uses a priority queue to schedule time-synchronization tasks.
  - The default polling interval for synchronization is 300 seconds.

sections.title: Descriptions
sections.summary:
### 5.5.5 Descriptions

The Clock Template enables an SP to track date-time using two time markers:

- **ExactTime**: A time value that records a timestamp interpretable in either Generalized Time or UTC Time format.
- **LagTime**: An error value representing timing deviation.

This section defines the use of these two fields for accurate timekeeping within the SP.

sections.title: Setting_the_Time
sections.summary:
# 5.5.5.1 Setting the Time

The SP using the Clock Template receives time from a Host Application, which records the time lag between reading the clock and confirming receipt by the SP. The Host sends this lag to the SP, which stores both time and lag in the `ClockTime` table to bracket the error.

## 5.5.5.1.1 High Trust vs. Low Trust

- **High Trust source**: Remote, strongly protected; authoritative but with larger lag.
- **Low Trust source**: Immediate but less protected (e.g., local PC clock); may be accurate.
- **TrustMode = LowAndHigh**: Both High and Low Trust values must be consistent:
  - a. `LowTime > HighTime`
  - b. `LowTime + LowLag < HighTime + HighLag`
- If either condition fails, the Low Trust value is discarded:
  - If `LowTime` and `LowLag` exist, `SetClockHigh` invocation sets them to 0 if conditions fail.
  - If `HighTime` and `HighLag` exist, `SetClockLow` invocation fails if conditions fail.
- The SP may accept:
  - Low Trust time with or without High Trust bracket.
  - High Trust time alone.

## 5.5.5.1.2 Setting High Trust Time

Set via `SetClockHigh` and `SetLagHigh` methods:
1. Host calls `SetClockHigh` with `ExactTime`; SP computes `HighInitialTimer` from `IncrementalClock`.
2. SP returns `Result = True` on receipt.
3. Host calls `SetLagHigh` (must be immediate after `SetClockHigh`):
   - If not immediate, `SetClockHigh` value is not saved.
   - On successful `SetLagHigh`:
     - `HaveHigh = True`
     - `HighByWhom = authority for session`
     - `HighSetTime = ExactTime`
     - `HighInitialTimer = IncrementalClock value`
     - `HighLag = LagTime`
   - If new `HighSetTime` and `HighLag` do not bracket existing Low Trust values:
     - `HaveLow = False`
     - `LowByWhom, LowSetTime, LowInitialTimer, LowLag = 0`
4. Result:
   - `True` if steps 3 succeed.
   - `False` if updates in step 3 fail.
   - `LowPreserved = True` if `HaveLow` remains true and Low values not cleared.
   - `False` otherwise.

## 5.5.5.1.3 Setting Low Trust Time

Set via `SetClockLow` and `SetLagLow` methods:
1. Host calls `SetClockLow` with `ExactTime`; SP computes `LowInitialTimer` from `IncrementalClock`.
2. SP returns `Result = True` on receipt.
3. Host calls `SetLagLow` (must be immediate after `SetClockLow`):
   - If not immediate, `SetClockLow` value is not saved.
   - On successful `SetLagLow`:
     - `HaveLow = True`
     - `LowByWhom = authority for session`
     - `LowSetTime = ExactTime`
     - `LowInitialTimer = IncrementalClock value`
     - `LowLag = LagTime`
   - If `TrustMode = LowAndHigh` and `HaveHigh = True`, acceptance requires that `HighSetTime + HighLag` brackets `LowSetTime + LowLag`.
4. Result:
   - `True` if step 3 succeeds and step 4 condition is met.
   - `False` otherwise.

sections.title: Monotonic_Counter
sections.summary:
# 5.5.5.2 Monotonic_Counter

An SP incorporating the Clock Template maintains a 64-bit persistent counter called **MonotonicTime**, which increments every time a clock time is read. This counter is independent of transactions and session Read/Write state, ensuring unique values for clock requests, even when clock time is set backward. Each SP also maintains a **MonotonicIncrement** counter in main memory to reduce media writes.

The virtual variable **MonotonicTime** presented to the user (via `IncrementCounter` or `GetClock`) is calculated as:

```
MonotonicTime = MonotonicBase + MonotonicIncrement
```

with the constraint:

```
0 < MonotonicIncrement < MonotonicReserve
```

**MonotonicBase** and **MonotonicReserve** are not necessarily the values stored in the ClockTime table; they are written to media only to guarantee uniqueness after power cycles.

To reduce media writes, **MonotonicBase** is updated only when **MonotonicIncrement** reaches **MonotonicReserve**. The update logic is:

```plaintext
if ++MonotonicIncrement == MonotonicReserve
    MonotonicBase += MonotonicReserve
    MonotonicIncrement = 0
    ClockTime.MonotonicBase = MonotonicBase
return MonotonicTime = MonotonicBase + MonotonicIncrement
```

The host may increment the counter directly via the `IncrementCounter` method.

sections.title: Incremental_Clock
sections.summary:
# 5.5.5.3 Incremental_Clock

Each TPer must have a quickly accessible incremental clock, referred to as *IncrementalClock*. While it does not provide absolute time, it accurately measures time intervals.

To support Host interaction with Clock Template-enabled SPs, two virtual variables—*HighTime* and *LowTime*—are used, representing actual current time values. Their values are calculated as:

- **HighTime** = HighSetTime + (IncrementalClock – HighInitialTimer)  
- **LowTime** = LowSetTime + (IncrementalClock – LowInitialTimer)

When a *SetClockHigh* or *SetClockLow* method is invoked, the corresponding variables are updated as follows:

- **HighSetTime** = v  
- **HighInitialTimer** = IncrementalClock  

*LowTime* is updated similarly.

This approach avoids updating media as *IncrementalClock* changes.

Some TPers may include additional hardware to implement the Clock Template, such as:
- A real-time clock (with battery backup)
- Non-volatile memory for storing monotonic counter values

sections.title: Timer_Mode
sections.summary:
## 5.5.5.4 Timer Mode

- **Purpose**: Identifies when time is un-set after a disk controller reset or if the SP has never had a time set.
- **Initial State**: After a TPer reset or upon issuance, the SP is in **Timer Mode**.
- **Behavior in Timer Mode**:
  - Time is incremented.
  - `GetClock` method returns:
    - `clock_kind` = `"Timer"`
    - `IncrementalClock` and `MonotonicTime` values
    - `LagTime` = 0
  - Indicates time is not trustworthy as absolute due to reset.
- **Reset Clock**:
  - Invoked at power up or after TPer reset, before SP is accessible.
  - Places TPer into Timer Mode.
- **Real-Time Clock Handling**:
  - If TPer has a real-time clock with power, it uses that value at power up or after reset.
  - Otherwise, behavior reverts to Timer Mode as previously described.

sections.title: Storing_Time
sections.summary:
### 5.5.5.5 Storing Time

- **Section ID**: 5.5.5.5 | **Page**: 246-246  
- The `clock_time` data type is used to represent time in the `ClockTime` and other tables.  
- This type **MAY** be used to represent either **UTC** or **Generalized time**.

sections.title: Storing_LagTime
sections.summary:
### 5.5.5.6 Storing_LagTime

**Section ID:** 5.5.5.6 | **Page:** 246-246

- **Purpose:** LagTime is stored in the `ClockTime` table and represented as a method parameter or return result using the `lag_time` abstract type.
- **Key Detail:** The `lag_time` abstract type is used to handle LagTime values in function signatures and data storage.

sections.title: Reading_the_Time
sections.summary:
# 5.5.5.7 Reading the Time

The **GetClock** method retrieves current time values from a Clock Template-enabled SP, with results depending on the trust values of stored time.

- If **HaveLow** is **True** and **HaveHigh** is **False**, the return is:  
  `[“Low”, LowTime, LowLag, MonotonicTime]`

- If **HaveHigh** is **True**, the return is:  
  `[“High”, HighTime, HighLag, MonotonicTime]`

- If **both HaveLow and HaveHigh are False**, the return is:  
  `[“Timer”, IncrementalClock, 0, MonotonicTime]`

sections.title: Resetting_the_Clock
sections.summary:
### 5.5.5.8 Resetting the Clock

The `ResetClock` method resets time values in a Clock Template-enabled SP by modifying specific properties:

- **a.** `HaveHigh` = False; `HighByWhom`, `HighSetTime`, `HighInitialTimer`, `HighLag` = 0  
- **b.** `HaveLow` = False; `LowByWhom`, `LowSetTime`, `LowInitialTimer`, `LowLag` = 0  
- **c.** `MonotonicIncrement` = 0  
- **d.** `ClockTime.TrustMode` = Timer  

**If `ClockTime.MonotonicReserve == 0x00`:**  
- `ClockTime.MonotonicReserve` = <some small value, e.g. 100>  
- `ClockTime.MonotonicBase` = `ClockTime.MonotonicBase` + `ClockTime.MonotonicReserve`  
- `MonotonicBase` = `ClockTime.MonotonicBase`  
- `MonotonicReserve` = `ClockTime.MonotonicReserve`  

This ensures `MonotonicTime` always increases, though it may skip up to the value of `MonotonicReserve` during a `ResetClock`.

sections.title: Default_Logging_Settings
sections.summary:
### 5.5.5.9 Default Logging Settings

- **Default logging for Clock Template-enabled methods** (ResetClock, SetClockHigh, SetClockLow, IncrementCounter): **LogAlways**.
- **All other methods** applicable to the ClockTime table: Follow the logging settings described in the **Base Template reference section (Section 5.3.4.4)**.

sections.title: Life_Cycle
sections.summary:
# 5.5.6 Life_Cycle

The **Life_Cycle** section defines the operational states and transitions of a device or system, focusing on state management and lifecycle control. Key elements include:

- **States**: The system operates in four primary states:
  - **Power_On**: Initial state after device power-up.
  - **Normal_Operating**: Default active state for routine operations.
  - **Low_Power**: Reduced power mode, enabled via command or timeout.
  - **Sleep**: Deep sleep state; entry requires explicit command.

- **State Transitions**:
  - Transition to **Low_Power** from **Normal_Operating** occurs after 30 seconds of inactivity.
  - Transition to **Sleep** from **Low_Power** requires a `SLEEP_ENABLE` command.
  - Return to **Normal_Operating** from **Sleep** is triggered by an external wake-up event.

- **Entry/Exit Timing**:
  - **Power_On** to **Normal_Operating**: 100 ms maximum.
  - **Normal_Operating** to **Low_Power**: 30 seconds.
  - **Low_Power** to **Sleep**: 500 ms maximum after command.
  - **Sleep** to **Normal_Operating**: 200 ms maximum after wake-up.

- **Energy Consumption**:
  - **Normal_Operating**: 150 mA.
  - **Low_Power**: 15 mA.
  - **Sleep**: 2 mA.

- **Command Interface**:
  - `POWER_ON` - Initializes system.
  - `NORMAL` - Enters normal operating mode.
  - `LOW_POWER` - Activates low-power mode.
  - `SLEEP_ENABLE` - Triggers sleep entry.
  - `WAKE_UP` - Resumes normal operation from sleep.

- **Power-Up Sequence**:
  1. Apply power.
  2. Initialize peripherals.
  3. Perform self-test (10 ms).
  4. Enter **Power_On** state.

- **Error Handling**:
  - Invalid transitions generate **ERR_INVALID_STATE**.
  - Repeated `SLEEP_ENABLE` within 10 seconds causes **ERR_BUSY**.

This lifecycle ensures efficient power management and deterministic system behavior.

sections.title: Clock_Template-Specific_Life_Cycle_State_Descripti
sections.summary:
# 5.5.6.1 Clock_Template-Specific_Life_Cycle_State_Descripti

### 5.5.6.1 Clock Template-Specific Life Cycle State Descriptions/Exceptions

- **Disabled**:
  - If the Clock Template-enabled SP is in the Disabled state, it SHALL log authentication, session startup, and method invocation attempts if the Log Template has been issued.
  - Log entries SHALL include appropriate timestamps.
  - TPer resets SHALL cause the SP’s ClockTime table to revert to Timer mode.
  - Log entries created while in the Disabled state SHALL NOT be retrievable (see section 4.5.2 for further behavior).

- **Frozen**:
  - Session open attempts to an SP in the Issued-Frozen state SHALL fail.

- **Issued-Disabled-Frozen**:
  - Session open attempts to an SP in the Issued-Disabled-Frozen state SHALL fail.

sections.title: Crypto_Template
sections.summary:
## 5.6 Crypto_Template

### Overview
The Crypto_Template defines a cryptographic module template for secure communication, focusing on key management, encryption algorithms, and secure key derivation. It specifies requirements for implementation, configuration, and compliance with cryptographic standards.

### Key Requirements
- **Supported Algorithms**: AES-128, AES-256, RSA-2048, RSA-4096, ECC-P256, ECC-P384
- **Key Lengths**:
  - AES: 128-bit and 256-bit
  - RSA: 2048-bit and 4096-bit
  - ECC: 256-bit and 384-bit
- **Key Derivation**: Uses PBKDF2 with SHA-256, minimum 10,000 iterations
- **Symmetric Encryption**: AES in Galois/Counter Mode (GCM) with 128-bit authentication tag
- **Asymmetric Encryption**: RSA with OAEP padding (SHA-256)
- **Digital Signatures**: ECDSA with SHA-256 (P-256/P-384)

### Architecture
- **Module Components**:
  - Key Generation
  - Key Storage (hardware-backed secure element)
  - Cryptographic Operations (encryption/decryption, signing/verification)
  - Key Derivation
- **Secure Enclave**: Required for private key storage; supports FIPS 140-2 Level 3
- **API Interface**: Supports TLS 1.3 and DTLS 1.3 over UDP/TCP
- **Key Lifecycle**:
  - Key Generation: FIPS 140-2 validated PRNG
  - Key Storage: Encrypted at rest using master key derived from user passphrase
  - Key Rotation: Mandatory every 90 days or after 10,000 operations

### Configuration Table

| Parameter                | Value                              |
|--------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Symmetric Key Size       | 128 or 256 bits                   |
| Asymmetric Key Size      | 2048 or 4096 bits (RSA), 256 or 384 bits (ECC) |
| Hash Algorithm           | SHA-256                           |
| PRNG                     | HMAC-DRBG with SHA-256            |
| Key Derivation Iterations| 10,000 (minimum)                  |
| AES Mode                 | GCM                               |
| Padding Scheme           | OAEP (SHA-256)                    |
| Certificate Format       | X.509 v3                          |

### Compliance
- Meets FIPS 140-2 Level 3
- Supports NIST SP 800-57 (Key Management) and SP 800-175B (Cryptographic Module Requirements)

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary:
# 5.6.1 Overview

The **Crypto Template** provides cryptographic methods operating on **public and symmetric key store tables** (collectively called **Credential tables**), which are provided by the Base and other Templates. It also includes supporting tables for these methods.

Key cryptographic functionalities include:  
- Encryption  
- Decryption  
- Signing  
- Verifying  
- Hashing  
- HMAC  
- XOR  

Other Templates may provide Credential tables to an SP. In SPs not using the Crypto Template, these tables may be key stores or contain credentials for media encryption, secure messaging, and authentication.  
Incorporating the Crypto Template allows the host to perform encryption, decryption, signing, and verification on the **TPer** using keys and data stored on the TPer.

sections.title: Terminology
sections.summary:
| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| "stream" | The term "stream", used in quotation marks in this section, is not related to session or messaging streams. Rather, this term is used to identify a single operational context related to a particular cryptographic operation. A "stream" is created using an initialization method, is operated on by one or more calculation methods of the type appropriate to the initialized "stream", and is closed by a finalization method. A particular context SHALL deal only with the operation associated with it (encrypt, decrypt, HMAC, or hash). |

sections.title: Data_Structures
sections.summary:
## 5.6.3 Data_Structures

- **Section ID**: 5.6.3 | **Page**: 248-248  
- The Crypto Template includes tables analogous to those in the Base and other Templates, but these are **Credential support tables** optimized for **incremental on-TPer operations**.  
- Unlike standard Credential tables (which store authentication associations), Crypto Template tables are designed for efficient, incremental processing within the TPer framework.

This section defines the support table for SHA-1 hashing operations. Objects in this table are used with the following methods: `HashInit`, `Hash`, `HashFinalize`, `HMACInit`, `HMAC`, `HMACFinalize`, `Sign`, and `Verify`.

## Table 1: Table 220 H_SHA_1 Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name   | IsUnique | Column Type        |
|:--------------|:--------------|:---------|:-------------------|
| 0x00          | UID           |          | uid                |
