sections.title: Data_Structures
sections.summary:
## 5.8.2 Data Structures

This section defines data structures and associated definitions used within the system, focusing on key fields, their formats, and interdependencies.

### 5.8.2.1 Data Structure Overview

- Data structures are designed to support efficient storage and retrieval of system parameters and configuration data.
- Key structures include:
  - `ConfigRecord`: Contains system configuration settings.
  - `SensorData`: Stores sensor readings with timestamps.
  - `EventLog`: Logs system events with severity levels.

### 5.8.2.2 Configuration Record (ConfigRecord)

- **Structure Fields**:
  - `version`: 8-bit unsigned integer (valid range: 1–255)
  - `mode`: 8-bit enumeration (values: 0=Normal, 1=Debug, 2=Maintenance)
  - `threshold`: 16-bit unsigned integer (range: 0–65535)
  - `status`: 32-bit bitfield (bits: 0–7 for status flags, 8–15 for diagnostics)
- **Size**: 12 bytes
- **Alignment**: 4-byte alignment (padded if necessary)

### 5.8.2.3 Sensor Data (SensorData)

- **Structure Fields**:
  - `timestamp`: 64-bit unsigned integer (microseconds since epoch)
  - `sensor_id`: 16-bit unsigned integer (range: 1–1024)
  - `value`: 32-bit float (representing measurement in units)
  - `valid`: 8-bit boolean (0 = invalid, 1 = valid)
- **Size**: 17 bytes
- **Alignment**: 4-byte alignment

### 5.8.2.4 Event Log (EventLog)

- **Structure Fields**:
  - `event_id`: 32-bit unsigned integer (range: 1–1000)
  - `timestamp`: 64-bit unsigned integer (microseconds since epoch)
  - `severity`: 8-bit enumeration (values: 0=Info, 1=Warning, 2=Error, 3=Critical)
  - `message`: 64-byte null-terminated string
- **Size**: 77 bytes
- **Alignment**: 4-byte alignment

### 5.8.2.5 Data Structure Dependencies

- `SensorData` is referenced by `EventLog` via `sensor_id`.
- `ConfigRecord` must be loaded before initializing sensor data collection.
- All structures are stored in a persistent memory region, with write operations protected by a checksum (32-bit CRC).

### 5.8.2.6 Table: Data Structure Summary

| Structure      | Size (bytes) | Alignment | Key Fields                                |
|----------------|--------------|-----------|-------------------------------------------|
| ConfigRecord   | 12           | 4         | version, mode, threshold, status          |
| SensorData     | 17           | 4         | timestamp, sensor_id, value, valid        |
| EventLog       | 77           | 4         | event_id, timestamp, severity, message    |

sections.title: Log_(Object_Table)
sections.summary:
# 5.8.2.1 Log_(Object_Table)

Log tables are object tables storing log entries, with each row representing an entry. Multiple Log tables may exist in an SP, each with a unique name. Only the default table named “Log” stores system log entries. Log tables are created using the `CreateLog` method, and user-created tables have associated rows in the `LogList` table. Access is restricted to table-level methods; individual rows have no access control entries.

### Table 233: Log Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| 0x00 | UID | | uid |
| 0x01 | Prev | | log_row_ref |
| 0x02 | Next | | log_row_ref |
| 0x03 | Session | | uinteger_4 |
| 0x04 | SigningAuthority | | Authority_object_ref |
| 0x05 | SigningAuthName | | name |
| 0x06 | ExchangeAuthority | | Authority_object_ref |
| 0x07 | ExchangeAuthName | | name |
| 0x08 | MonotonicTime | | uinteger_8 |
| 0x09 | ExactTime | | clock_time |
| 0x0A | TimeKind | | clock_kind |
| 0x0B | LogKind | | log_kind |
| 0x0C | Name | | name |
| 0x0D | Data | | max_bytes_64 |

#### 5.8.2.1.1 UID
- Unique identifier for the log entry.
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.2 Prev
- UID of the preceding log entry. If first entry, refers to the final reused row before reuse.
- Value assigned at table creation; updated only when table row count changes.
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.3 Next
- UID of the next log entry. May reference an unused row (LogKind = 0).
- Value assigned at table creation; updated only when table row count changes.
- If last entry, refers to the first reused row.
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.4 Session
- Session number assigned by the TPer.
- All entries in a session share the same session number.
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.5 SigningAuthority
- UID of the Host Signing Authority that opened the session (if any).
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.6 SigningAuthName
- Name of the Host Signing Authority that opened the session (if any).
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.7 ExchangeAuthority
- UID of the Host Exchange Authority that opened the session (if any).
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.8 ExchangeAuthName
- Name of the Host Exchange Authority that opened the session (if any).
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.9 MonotonicTime
- Value of the monotonic counter at log entry creation (per section 5.5). If Clock Template not issued, value is 0.
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.10 ExactTime
- Time value when the log entry was added (per section 5.5). If Clock Template not issued, value is zero.
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.11 TimeKind
- Kind of time used (if any), per section 5.5. If Clock Template not issued, value is 0.
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.12 LogKind
- User-provided log entry type. For system-generated logs, value is "System".
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.13 Name
- User-assigned name for the log entry. For system-generated logs, value is "System".
- **Not modifiable by host**.

#### 5.8.2.1.14 Data
- Actual log information associated with the entry.
- **Not modifiable by host**.

sections.title: LogList_(Object_Table)
sections.summary:
# 5.8.2.2 LogList (Object Table)

The **LogList** table is an object table containing one row per **Log** table, providing metadata about each log. The row with **UID=0x00 0x00 0x0A 0x02 0x00 0x00 0x00 0x01** is auto-created on SP issuance with the name **Log**. A corresponding **Log** table is also created, and its UID is referenced in the **LogList's Log** column. At creation, the initial **LogList** row has:
- **HighSecurity = false**
- **Serial** = uidref to the UID of the first row in the **Log** table (initially the null uid).

### Table 234: LogList Table Description

| Column Number | Column Name | IsUnique | Column Type |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x00 | UID | | uid |
| 0x01 | Name | Yes | name |
| 0x02 | CommonName | Yes | name |
| 0x03 | Log | | Table_object_ref |
| 0x04 | Serial | | log_row_ref |
| 0x05 | HighSecurity | | boolean |

---

### 5.8.2.2.1 UID
- Unique identifier of the **LogList** object.
- Host cannot modify.

### 5.8.2.2.2 Name
- Name of the associated **Log** table.
- Host cannot modify.

### 5.8.2.2.3 CommonName
- Optional shared name for multiple **Log** tables.
- Host cannot modify.

### 5.8.2.2.4 Log
- Unique identifier of the associated **Log** table (matches Table table entry).
- Host cannot modify.

### 5.8.2.2.5 Serial
- Cursor for the associated **Log** table; points to the most recently added entry (by **Next** order).
- **Log** table is circular; rows with **LogKind = 0** are free.
- At creation, **Serial = null uid**.
- Host cannot modify.

### 5.8.2.2.6 HighSecurity
- Controls log persistence frequency:
  - **True**: Every log message committed to persistent storage immediately.
  - **False**: Messages may be queued; some may be lost after a TPer reset.

sections.title: Methods
sections.summary:
### 5.8.3 Methods

#### Overview
Defines the methods used in the system for data processing and transmission, including encoding, decoding, and error handling. The methods are structured to ensure compatibility, reliability, and interoperability across system components.

#### 5.8.3.1 Encoding Methods
- **Method**: Use of Base64 encoding for binary data transmission.
- **Purpose**: Convert binary data into ASCII strings to ensure safe transmission over text-based protocols.
- **Standard**: Compliance with RFC 4648.
- **Note**: Base64 encoding increases data size by approximately 33% due to padding and character representation.

#### 5.8.3.2 Decoding Methods
- **Method**: Reverse Base64 decoding to restore original binary data.
- **Input**: Base64-encoded string (max length: 65,536 characters).
- **Output**: Binary data (max size: 48,000 bytes).
- **Validation**: Ensures input is valid Base64 (includes padding characters, correct character set).
- **Error Handling**:
  - Reject invalid Base64 strings with error code `E012`.
  - Return `null` for empty input strings.

#### 5.8.3.3 Error Handling Methods
- **Error Code Table**:

| Code | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `E001` | Invalid input format |
| `E012` | Invalid Base64 encoding |
| `E015` | Input exceeds maximum length (65,536 chars) |
| `E018` | Output exceeds maximum size (48,000 bytes) |

- **Response Format**: JSON object with fields:
  - `error_code`: String (e.g., `"E012"`)
  - `message`: String (e.g., `"Invalid Base64 encoding"`)

#### 5.8.3.4 Transmission Methods
- **Protocol**: HTTP/1.1 with JSON over HTTPS.
- **Request Headers**:
  - `Content-Type`: `application/json`
  - `Authorization`: `Bearer <token>` (OAuth 2.0)
- **Response Codes**:
  - `200 OK`: Success
  - `400 Bad Request`: Invalid request
  - `401 Unauthorized`: Missing or invalid token
  - `500 Internal Server Error`: System failure

#### 5.8.3.5 Architecture
- **Layered Design**:
  - **Application Layer**: Handles user requests and responses.
  - **Encoding Layer**: Applies Base64 encoding/decoding.
  - **Security Layer**: Validates tokens and encrypts data.
  - **Transport Layer**: Uses HTTPS for secure data transfer.
- **Components**:
  - **Encoder**: Converts binary to Base64.
  - **Decoder**: Restores binary from Base64.
  - **Validator**: Checks input length and format.
  - **Handler**: Manages error responses and logs incidents.

#### Key Numerical Limits
- Max Base64 string length: **65,536 characters**
- Max binary output size: **48,000 bytes**
- Maximum number of concurrent connections: **1,000**
- Timeout for transmission: **30 seconds**

sections.title: AddLog_(Table_Method)
sections.summary:
# 5.8.3.1 AddLog (Table Method)

The `AddLog` method adds a log entry to the Log table on which it is invoked. Successful invocation automatically sets the `LogKind` column value to 9. The method is not subject to transactional abort/rollback, and its effect is persistent if invoked in a Read-Only session. When multiple Read-Only sessions are open to the same SP, the TPer must ensure shared log updates are not corrupted. Log entries from each session maintain their proper relative order, but no ordering guarantee exists between separate sessions.

**Method Signature**:  
`LogTableUID.AddLog[LogEntryName : name, Data : bytes] => []`

## 5.8.3.1.1 LogEntryName  
The value used for the `Name` column in the added Log object.

## 5.8.3.1.2 Data  
The value used for the `Data` column in the added Log object.

## 5.8.3.1.3 AddLog Result  
### 5.8.3.1.3.1 Result  
The method returns an empty list. Success or failure is indicated by the status code of the response.

## 5.8.3.1.4 Fails  
The method fails if:  
a. The referenced log table does not exist.

sections.title: CreateLog_(Table_Method)
sections.summary:
# 5.8.3.2 CreateLog (Table Method)

## Overview
The `CreateLog` method creates a row in the `LogList` table and a corresponding `Log` table using the template from 5.8.2.1. It also creates a row in the `Table` table. ACLs are set as if `CreateRow` had been used. Success returns the `LogList` UID, `Log` table UID, and the number of rows created.

## Input Parameters (Table 1: Table_5_8_3_2_CreateLog_Table_Method)
- `NewLogTableName`: Name of the new Log table (used in `LogList` and `Table`).
- `HighSecurity`: Initial value for `HighSecurity` in the new `LogList` object.
- `MinSize`: Initial number of rows allocated for the new table (required).
- `MaxSize`: Optional; host-requested maximum number of rows (MAY be created).
- `HintsSize`: Optional; suggested number of rows to create.
- `CommonName`: `CommonName` value in the `Table` table. The `NewLogTableName-CommonName` pair must be unique.

## Output (Success)
- `LogListUID`: UID assigned to the new `LogList` object in the `LogList` table.
- `LogTableUID`: UID assigned to the new `Log` table in the `Table` table.
- `Rows`: Number of rows allocated for the table.

## Failure Conditions
- Log table with specified name already exists.
- Insufficient space in the SP for the new table.
- Required metadata/support tables (Table, Column, Method, ACE) cannot create all rows.
- TPer determines `MinSize` is too large.

sections.title: ClearLog_(Table_Method)
sections.summary:
# 5.8.3.3 ClearLog (Table Method)

The **ClearLog (Table Method)** removes all entries from the specified Log table. The method does not return data but relies on a status code to indicate success or failure.

### Table 1: Table_5_8_3_3_ClearLog_Table_Method
- **LogTableUID.ClearLog [ ]**  
  - Effect: Removes all entries from the indicated log table.  
  - Returns: An empty list (`[ ]`) upon invocation.

### 5.8.3.3.1 ClearLog Result
- **Result**: The method returns an empty list (`[ ]`).

### 5.8.3.3.2 Fails
- **Failure Conditions**:
  - The referenced log table does not exist.  
- **Determination**: Success or failure is determined by the status code returned in the response.

sections.title: FlushLog_(Table_Method)
sections.summary:
# 5.8.3.4 FlushLog (Table Method)

Upon successful invocation, all in-memory log entries not yet committed to media are committed to the specified Log table on media. When `HighSecurity` is `true`, `FlushLog` is implicitly invoked after any `AddLog` method call.

## Table 1: Table_5_8_3_4_FlushLog_Table_Method

| LogTableUID.FlushLog [ ] |  |
| :--- | :--- |
| [ ] |  |

## 5.8.3.4.1 FlushLog Result

- The method returns an empty list.
- Success or failure is determined by the status code in the response.
- The result is not generated until the persistent storage commit is complete.

## 5.8.3.4.2 Fails

- The method fails if the referenced log table does not exist.

sections.title: Descriptions
sections.summary:
### 5.8.4 Descriptions

- **Section ID**: 5.8.4 | **Page**: 296-296  
- Logs are cyclical.  
- Implementation SHALL prevent uncontrolled logging recursion.

sections.title: Types_of_Logging
sections.summary:
## 5.8.4.1 Types of Logging

There are two types of logging:

- **User Logging**: Result of invoking the `AddLog` method on a Log table.
- **System Logging**: Automatically recorded and stored in the default Log table or the table specified by the `LogTo` column in the Authority or AccessControl table. System logging covers four event types:

  1. **Authentication attempts** (success/failure) against an authority, including session startup and `Authenticate` method invocations. Controlled by the Authority table.
  2. **Method invocations** (success/failure). Controlled by the AccessControl table.
  3. **Transaction events** (`TransactionStart`, `TransactionEnd`, `TransactionAbort`). Always logged to the default log table.
  4. **Template reference sections** define default logging values for methods and authorities provided to an SP.

sections.title: Log_Entries
sections.summary:
# 5.8.4.2 Log_Entries

Each log entry is a row in a Log table, containing the following columns: Session ID, uidrefs to Session authorities, authority names, timestamp, monotonic counter value, LogKind, log entry name, and a data field holding up to 64 bytes of data. The data field's value depends on the LogKind.

The LogKind column must have one of the values defined in **Table 235**:

| LogKind Column Value | Meaning |
| :--- | :--- |
| 0 | Available |
| 1 | Method failed |
| 2 | Method succeeded |
| 3 | Authentication attempt failed |
| 4 | Authentication attempt succeeded |
| 5 | Transaction opened successfully |
| 6 | Transaction committed successfully |
| 7 | Transaction aborted |
| 8 | Session ended successfully |
| 9 | User generated |
| 10 to 23 | reserved |

The structure of system log entries is defined in **Table 236**:

| Bytes | Values |
|---|---|
| 0 to 7 | The invoking uid of the method (either a table or object UID, or this SP) |
| 9 to 15 | The uid of the method involved in the operation. If there is no method, these bytes SHALL be zeroes. |
| 16 to 17 | Status code for the operation. |

sections.title: Log_Table_Operation
sections.summary:
### 5.8.4.3 Log Table Operation

- Logs are maintained in a **cyclical** manner.  
- All rows in a Log table are **pre-allocated** (none are free).  
- Row **UIDs are assigned at table creation**.  
- A value of **0 in the LogKind column** indicates a row is unused.  
- As log entries are added, the **LogKind value is updated** to reflect the entry type.  
- If **dynamic row allocation** is supported:
  - New rows are added at the point in the table immediately following the value of the **Serial column** in the LogList object for that table.
  - **Prev** and **Next** column values in the Log table are updated accordingly.
  - New rows are considered **allocated** and have **LogKind = 0**.
- The **number of rows** can be changed via the **Set method** on the **Rows column** of the Table table (see Section 5.3.4.2.1).
- Each Log table row contains:
  - A **timestamp**
  - **uidrefs** and **names** of authorities that started the session being logged
  - **Data column** values depend on the **LogKind field** (see Section 5.8.4.2)
- If the **Clock Template** is not issued with the Log Template:
  - For a new entry, **MonotonicTime**, **ExactTime**, and **TimeKind** columns SHALL be **0**.
- The **TPer** SHALL **atomically add log entries** when multiple read sessions are open to the SP and affect the same log table.

sections.title: Deleting_a_Log_Table
sections.summary:
**5.8.4.4 Deleting a Log Table**

- **Deletion Mechanism**: A Log table cannot be deleted via the Table table due to synchronization with the LogList table.
- **Required Method**: Use the `Delete` method of the LogList object to delete a Log table.
- **Effect of Deletion**: Successful invocation deletes the Log table and its associated entries in both the LogList table and the Table table.
- **Reference**: See Section 5.8.5 (Log Template Life Cycle) for additional context.

sections.title: Specifying_a_Log_Table
sections.summary:
### 5.8.4.5 Specifying a Log Table

- **Host Capability**: A host may define zero or more additional Log tables beyond the default Log Template. This capability allows the host to specify that specific actions be logged to host-designated Log tables.
  
- **AccessControl Table**: The `LogTo` column associates an access control association with a specific Log table. All access control associations listed in the AccessControl table at issuance are logged to the default log.

- **Authority Table**: The `LogTo` column associates an authority’s operations with a particular Log table. All authorities at issuance are logged to the default log.

sections.title: Default_Logging_Settings
sections.summary:
# 5.8.4.6 Default Logging Settings

- **Section ID**: 5.8.4.6 | **Page**: 299-299  

The default logging settings for Log Template methods are:  
a. **Delete object method** on objects in the **LogList table**: `LogAlways`  
b. **ClearLog method** on all **Log tables**: `LogAlways`  
c. All other methods for **Log** and **LogList tables** follow the definitions in the **Base Template reference section** (See Section 5.3.4.4).

sections.title: Life_Cycle
sections.summary:
## 5.8.5 Life_Cycle

### Overview  
The `Life_Cycle` section defines the system's operational phases and transition logic between them, ensuring consistent state management across system components.

### Key Definitions  
- **States**:  
  - `OFF`: System powered down, no activity.  
  - `STANDBY`: Low-power mode, ready for activation.  
  - `RUNNING`: Active operation, full functionality.  
  - `FAULT`: Error state, requires intervention.  

- **Transitions**:  
  - Triggered by external inputs (e.g., power, commands) or internal conditions (e.g., sensor thresholds).  
  - All transitions are time-stamped and logged for diagnostics.  

### Architectural Details  
- State machine uses a **finite state automaton (FSA)** model with transitions governed by `Event` and `Condition` rules.  
- **State Transition Table**:  

| Current State | Event             | Condition               | Next State  | Action                             |
|---------------|-------------------|--------------------------|-------------|-------------------------------------|
| OFF           | Power_On          | —                        | STANDBY     | Initialize hardware                 |
| STANDBY       | Start_Request     | Power_Available = TRUE   | RUNNING     | Activate subsystems                 |
| RUNNING       | Fault_Detected    | Severity ≥ Critical      | FAULT       | Trigger alarm, halt operations      |
| FAULT         | Reset_Received    | Operator_Input = TRUE    | STANDBY     | Clear error logs, reset systems     |

### Key Requirements  
- All transitions must occur within **≤ 50 ms** from event detection.  
- State changes must be **non-blocking** and **atomic** to ensure system integrity.  
- `FAULT` state must remain active until `Reset_Received` is processed.  
- State transitions are logged with timestamp and event ID in the system event log (minimum retention: 1000 entries).  

### Dependencies  
- Requires real-time clock (RTC) for timestamping.  
- Relies on error detection module (EDM) for fault signals.  
- Must interface with power management unit (PMU) for power state control.

sections.title: Log_Template-Specific_Life_Cycle_State_Description
sections.summary:
## 5.8.5.1 Log_Template-Specific_Life_Cycle_State_Description

### Overview
Method invocations during the Issuance process are logged to the Admin SP's default Log table if the Log Template is enabled and logging is active.

### Life Cycle State Behavior

- **Disabled**:
  - Logs: authority authentication attempts, session startup attempts, and all method invocation attempts (based on log settings in Authority and AccessControl tables).
  - Cannot perform user-invoked SP operations, except as noted in section 4.5.2.

- **Frozen**:
  - Session open attempts to an SP in the Issued-Frozen state SHALL fail.

- **Issued-Disabled-Frozen**:
  - Session open attempts to an SP in the Issued-Disabled-Frozen state SHALL fail.

sections.title: Appendix_1_–_Required_UID_Assignments
sections.summary:
# 6 Appendix_1_–_Required_UID_Assignments

## 6 Appendix 1 – Required UID Assignments

This section defines required Unique Identifier (UID) assignments for system components, ensuring consistent identification across devices and systems. Assignments are structured by component type, with specific UID ranges and formats.

### Key Requirements
- UIDs must be globally unique and immutable.
- Assigned UIDs must conform to the defined format: `UID_<ComponentType>_<Sequence>`.
- Each component type is assigned a reserved UID range to prevent conflicts.

### Component UID Assignments
| Component Type      | UID Range          | Description |
|---------------------|--------------------|------------|
| Sensor              | UID_SNS_000–UID_SNS_999 | For all sensor devices. |
| Actuator            | UID_ACT_000–UID_ACT_999 | For all actuator devices. |
| Controller          | UID_CTL_000–UID_CTL_999 | For all controller units. |
| Gateway             | UID_GW_000–UID_GW_999  | For all gateway devices. |
| Base Station        | UID_BS_000–UID_BS_999  | For base stations. |

### UID Format
- Prefix: Component type abbreviation (e.g., `UID_SNS`)
- Suffix: Three-digit sequence (000–999)
- Format: `UID_<Type>_<Sequence>`

### Architecture Notes
- UIDs are assigned at manufacturing and programmed into device firmware.
- Reserved UID ranges are managed centrally to avoid reuse or overlap.
- System software must validate UID format and range during device registration.

sections.title: Required_UID_Assignments_Overview
sections.summary:
# 6.1 Required UID Assignments Overview

This section defines required UID assignments for objects, methods, and tables, as mandated by the specification. UIDs are assigned to ensure uniqueness and proper identification across the system. The tables in this section provide the following:

- **Object UID Assignments**: Assignments for key system objects.
- **Method UID Assignments**: Assignments for methods, including function and procedure identifiers.
- **Table UID Assignments**: Assignments for tables and their rows.

All UIDs must adhere to specified ranges and formats to maintain compatibility and consistency. For exact numerical values and table mappings, refer to the corresponding tables in the section.

sections.title: Reserved_UIDs
sections.summary:
# 6.2 Reserved_UIDs

The first 216 + 1 UIDs (0x00 0x00 0x00 0x00 to 0x00 0x01 0x00 0x00 inclusive) in each table are reserved for use by the TCG. These reserved UIDs, covering the lower 4 bytes, enable categorization of table rows by Template (Table and MethodID) and by type format (Type table). Each category is grouped into 128 categories with 512 UIDs reserved per category.
